title.en: Volume 58 Biographies 23: Ming Kerang, Wei Dan, Lu Shuang, Du Taiqing,Xin Deyuan, Liu Bian, Xu ShanXin, Li Wenbo

sentences.zh: 明克讓明克讓，字弘道，平原鬲人也。

translations.literal: Ming Kerang, styled Hongdao, was a native of Ge in Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Kerang, whose style name was Hongdao, came from Ge in Pingyuan commandery.

sentences.zh: 父山賓，梁侍中。

translations.literal: His father Shanbin was an Attendant-in-ordinary of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shanbin had served Liang as Attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 克讓少好儒雅，善談論，博涉書史，所覽將萬卷。

translations.literal: Kerang from youth loved refined learning, was skilled at discourse, broadly traversed books and histories, and had read nearly ten thousand scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Kerang delighted in classical learning, excelled in conversation, and ranged widely through books and histories until he had read nearly ten thousand scrolls.

sentences.zh: 《三禮》禮論，尤所研精，龜策曆象，咸得其妙。

translations.literal: The Three Rites and ritual discourse he especially studied to mastery; tortoise divination, milfoil, calendars, and astral phenomena—he grasped the subtlety of them all.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself above all to the Three Rites and ritual theory, and in tortoise and milfoil divination, calendrics, and astronomy he mastered every subtle point.

sentences.zh: 年十四，釋褐湘東王法曹參軍。

translations.literal: At age fourteen he doffed commoner's garb and became Legal Bureau Attendant to the Prince of Xiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he entered office as Legal Bureau Attendant on the staff of the Prince of Xiangdong.

sentences.zh: 時舍人朱異在儀賢堂講《老子》，克讓預焉。

translations.literal: At that time the Palace Attendant Zhu Yi was lecturing on the Laozi in the Hall for Honoring the Worthy, and Kerang was present.
translations.idiomatic: About that time Palace Attendant Zhu Yi was lecturing on the Laozi in the Hall for Honoring the Worthy, and Kerang was among those present.

sentences.zh: 堂邊有修竹，異令克讓詠之。

translations.literal: Beside the hall were tall bamboos; Yi ordered Kerang to compose a poem on them.
translations.idiomatic: Tall bamboo grew beside the hall, and Yi asked Kerang to compose a poem on it.

sentences.zh: 克讓攬筆輒成，其卒章曰：「非君多愛賞，誰貴此貞心。

translations.literal: Kerang took up the brush and at once finished it; the closing couplet read: "Were it not for your great love and esteem, who would prize this steadfast heart?"
translations.idiomatic: Kerang took up his brush and finished the piece on the spot; its closing lines ran, "Were it not for your discerning favor, who would value this steadfast heart?"

sentences.zh: 」異甚奇之。

translations.literal: " Yi was greatly struck by it.
translations.idiomatic: " Yi was deeply impressed.

sentences.zh: 仕歷司徒祭酒、尚書都官郎中、散騎侍郎，兼國子博士、中書侍郎。

translations.literal: In office he successively served as Libationer of the Minister of Works, Director of the Bureau of Punishments in the Secretariat, Gentleman Cavalier Attendant, and concurrently as Erudite of the Imperial Academy and Attendant of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In his career he held the posts of Libationer under the Minister of Works, Director of the Bureau of Punishments in the Secretariat, and Gentleman Cavalier Attendant, while also serving concurrently as Erudite of the Imperial Academy and Secretariat Attendant.

sentences.zh: 梁滅，歸於長安，周明帝引為麟趾殿學士，俄授著作上士，轉外史下大夫，出為衛王友，歷漢東、南陳二郡守。

translations.literal: When Liang perished he went to Chang'an; Emperor Ming of Zhou summoned him as a scholar of the Linzhi Hall, soon appointed him Senior Compiler, then transferred him to Junior Grand Historian, sent out as Companion to the Prince of Wei, and served successively as prefect of the two commanderies of Handong and Nanchen.
translations.idiomatic: After Liang fell he made his way to Chang'an, where Emperor Ming of Zhou took him on as a scholar of the Linzhi Hall. He was soon made Senior Compiler, then promoted to Junior Grand Historian, later sent out as Companion to the Prince of Wei, and served in turn as prefect of Handong and Nanchen.

sentences.zh: 武帝即位，復徵為露門學士，令與太史官屬正定新曆。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu took the throne he was again summoned as a Lumengate scholar and ordered, together with officials of the Grand Astrologer's office, to fix the new calendar.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu came to the throne Kerang was summoned back as a Lumengate scholar and charged, together with the staff of the Grand Astrologer's office, to establish the new calendar.

sentences.zh: 拜儀同三司，累遷司調大夫，賜爵曆城縣伯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: He was appointed Commissioner with the Protocol of the Three Dukes, promoted in stages to Grand Master of Court Regulation, and enfeoffed as Baron of Licheng county with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He received appointment as Commissioner with Protocol Equal to the Three Dukes, rose through successive promotions to Grand Master of Court Regulation, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Licheng with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，拜太子內舍人，轉率更令，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication he was appointed Inner Gentleman of the Heir Apparent, transferred to Director of Palace Works, and advanced in rank to Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu accepted the throne he was made Inner Gentleman to the Heir Apparent, then transferred to Director of Palace Works and raised to the rank of Marquis.

sentences.zh: 太子以師道處之，恩禮甚厚。

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent treated him with the courtesy due a teacher, and his favor and ritual observance were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince treated him with the deference owed a teacher, and showed him exceptional favor and courtesy.

sentences.zh: 每有四方珍味，輒以賜之。

translations.literal: Whenever there were rare delicacies from the four quarters, he would always bestow them on him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever rare delicacies arrived from the four quarters, the prince would send them to him.

sentences.zh: 于時東宮盛征天下才學之士，至於博物洽聞，皆出其下。

translations.literal: At that time the Eastern Palace greatly recruited men of talent and learning from throughout the realm; as for broad knowledge and comprehensive learning, all were beneath him.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Palace at that time was recruiting learned men from across the empire, yet in breadth of learning and erudition none could match him.

sentences.zh: 詔與太常牛弘等修禮議樂，當朝典故多所裁正。

translations.literal: He was ordered together with the Minister of Rites Niu Hong and others to revise ritual and deliberate on music; many precedents of the current court he corrected and settled.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed him, together with Minister of Rites Niu Hong and others, to revise ritual and music, and he corrected a great many precedents then in use at court.

sentences.zh: 開皇十四年，以疾去官，加通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Kaihuang he left office on account of illness and was given the additional title of Regular Attendant of Direct and Unimpeded Service.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang 14 he resigned on account of illness and was given the additional title of Regular Attendant of Direct and Unimpeded Service.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: 上甚傷惜焉，賻物五百段，米三百石。

translations.literal: The emperor was deeply grieved; funeral gifts were five hundred bolts of goods and three hundred piculs of grain.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him deeply and sent five hundred bolts of goods and three hundred piculs of grain as funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 太子又贈絹布二千匹，錢十萬，朝服一具，給棺槨。

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent also gave two thousand bolts of silk and cloth, one hundred thousand in cash, one set of court robes, and supplied coffin and inner casket.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince added two thousand bolts of silk and cloth, one hundred thousand cash, a full set of court robes, and provided the coffin and inner casket.

sentences.zh: 著《孝經義疏》一部，《古今帝代記》一卷，《文類》四卷，《續名僧記》一卷，集二十卷。

translations.literal: He authored one work of Exegesis on the Classic of Filial Piety, one scroll of Record of Emperors Ancient and Modern, four scrolls of Literary Categories, one scroll of Continued Record of Eminent Monks, and collected writings in twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: His writings included an Exegesis on the Classic of Filial Piety, a Record of Emperors Ancient and Modern in one scroll, Literary Categories in four scrolls, a Continued Record of Eminent Monks in one scroll, and collected works in twenty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 子餘慶，官至司門郎。

translations.literal: His son Yuqing reached the office of Gate Master.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuqing rose to the post of Gate Master.

sentences.zh: 越王侗稱制，為國子祭酒。

translations.literal: When Prince of Yue Tong assumed regency, he became Libationer of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Yue Yang Tong held the regency, Yuqing served as Libationer of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 魏澹魏澹，字彥深，巨鹿下曲陽人也。

translations.literal: Wei Dan, styled Yanshen, was a native of Xiaquyang in Julu.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Dan, whose style name was Yanshen, came from Xiaquyang in Julu commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖鸞，魏光州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Luan was Governor of Guangzhou under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Luan had been Governor of Guangzhou under Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 父季景，齊大司農卿，稱為著姓，世以文學自業。

translations.literal: His father Jijing was Grand Minister of Agriculture under Qi; the clan was called an eminent surname, and for generations they took literature as their profession.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jijing served Qi as Grand Minister of Agriculture; the family was reckoned a distinguished clan that had pursued letters for generations.

sentences.zh: 澹年十五而孤，專精好學，博涉經史，善屬文，詞采贍逸。

translations.literal: Dan at fifteen was orphaned; he devoted himself to concentrated study, broadly traversed the classics and histories, was skilled at composition, and his diction was rich and flowing.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned at fifteen, Dan threw himself into study, ranged widely through the classics and histories, wrote with ease, and his prose was lush and fluent.

sentences.zh: 齊博陵王濟聞其名，引為記室。

translations.literal: The Prince of Boling Ji of Qi heard his name and summoned him as Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Boling, Ji of Qi, heard of him, he took Dan on as Recorder.

sentences.zh: 及琅邪王儼為京畿大都督，以澹為鎧曹參軍，轉殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Langye Yan became Metropolitan Commander of the Capital Region, he made Dan Armor Bureau Attendant, then transferred him to Palace Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Langye Yan became Metropolitan Commander of the Capital Region, he appointed Dan Armor Bureau Attendant and later transferred him to Palace Attendant Censor.

sentences.zh: 尋與尚書左僕射魏收、吏部尚書陽休之、國子博士熊安生同修《五禮》。

translations.literal: Soon, together with Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Wei Shou, Minister of Personnel Yang Xiuzhi, and Erudite Xiong Ansheng, he jointly compiled the Five Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He soon joined Left Vice Director Wei Shou, Minister of Personnel Yang Xiuzhi, and Erudite Xiong Ansheng in compiling the Five Rites.

sentences.zh: 又與諸學士撰《御覽》，書成，除殿中郎中、中書舍人。

translations.literal: He also joined various scholars in compiling the Imperial Overview; when the book was finished he was appointed Director in the Palace Bureau and Secretariat Draftsman.
translations.idiomatic: He also worked with other scholars on the Imperial Overview, and when that work was complete he was made Director in the Palace Bureau and Secretariat Draftsman.

sentences.zh: 復與李德林俱修國史。

translations.literal: He again joined Li Delin in compiling the national history.
translations.idiomatic: He again collaborated with Li Delin on the national history.

sentences.zh: 周武帝平齊，授納言中士。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou pacified Qi, he was appointed Senior Clerk of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu of Zhou conquered Qi, Dan was appointed Senior Clerk of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 及高祖受禪，出為行台禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication he was sent out as Vice Director of the Rites Bureau of the Field Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne Dan was sent out as Vice Director of the Rites Bureau on the Field Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 尋為散騎常侍、聘陳主使。

translations.literal: Soon he became Regular Attendant Cavalier and chief envoy on a mission to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Regular Attendant Cavalier and chief envoy on a mission to Chen.

sentences.zh: 還除太子舍人。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he was appointed Attendant to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 廢太子勇深禮遇之，屢加優錫，令注《庾信集》，復撰《笑苑》、《詞林集》，世稱其博物。

translations.literal: The deposed Heir Apparent Yong treated him with deep courtesy, repeatedly bestowing special gifts; he was ordered to annotate the Collected Works of Yu Xin, and also compiled the Garden of Laughter and the Forest of Phrases; the age praised his broad learning.
translations.idiomatic: The deposed crown prince Yong treated him with great respect and showered him with favors, commissioning him to annotate Yu Xin's collected works and to compile the Garden of Laughter and the Forest of Phrases; contemporaries acclaimed his encyclopedic learning.

sentences.zh: 數年，遷著作郎，仍為太子學士。

translations.literal: After several years he was transferred to Compiler, and still served as a scholar of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was promoted to Compiler while continuing as a scholar in the heir apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 高祖以魏收所撰書褒貶失實，平繪為《中興書》事不倫序，詔澹別成《魏史》。

translations.literal: Gaozu, because the book Wei Shou had compiled was untrue in its praise and blame, and Ping Hui's Zhongxing shu was disorderly in its arrangement of events, ordered Dan separately to complete a History of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu found Wei Shou's history unreliable in its judgments and Ping Hui's Book of the Restoration disorderly in its arrangement of events, and ordered Dan to compile a separate History of Wei.

sentences.zh: 澹自道武下及恭帝，為十二紀，七十八傳，別為史論及例一卷，並《目錄》合九十二卷。

translations.literal: Dan, from Emperor Daowu down to Emperor Gong, made twelve annals and seventy-eight biographies, with a separate scroll of historical discourse and precedents, together with a Table of Contents—in all ninety-two scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Dan's history ran from Emperor Daowu through Emperor Gong in twelve annals and seventy-eight biographies, with a separate scroll of historical discourse and precedents and a table of contents, ninety-two scrolls in all.

sentences.zh: 澹之義例與魏收多所不同：

translations.literal: Dan's principles of composition differed in many respects from those of Wei Shou:
translations.idiomatic: Dan's historiographical principles differed in many ways from Wei Shou's:

sentences.zh: 其一曰，臣聞天子者，繼天立極，終始絕名。

translations.literal: The first says: Your subject has heard that the Son of Heaven, succeeding Heaven and establishing the ultimate pole, from beginning to end is without personal name.
translations.idiomatic: The first principle: I have heard that the Son of Heaven, who succeeds Heaven and establishes the cosmic pole, is never recorded by personal name from first to last.

sentences.zh: 故《穀梁傳》曰：「太上不名。

translations.literal: Therefore the Guliang Commentary says: "The Supreme One is not named."
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Guliang Commentary says, "The Supreme One is not named."

sentences.zh: 」《曲禮》曰：「天子不言出，諸侯不生名。

translations.literal: " The Record of Rites says: "The Son of Heaven does not speak of going forth; feudal lords are not named at birth."
translations.idiomatic: " The Record of Rites says, "The Son of Heaven is not said to 'go forth'; feudal lords are not named at birth."

sentences.zh: 」諸侯尚不生名，況天子乎！

translations.literal: " If even feudal lords are not named at birth, how much more the Son of Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: " If even feudal lords go unnamed at birth, how much more the Son of Heaven!

sentences.zh: 若為太子，必須書名。

translations.literal: If one is the heir apparent, the name must be written.
translations.idiomatic: When the subject is the heir apparent, the name must be recorded.

sentences.zh: 良由子者對父生稱，父前子名，禮之意也。

translations.literal: This is truly because the son, facing the father, is called by his birth name; before the father the son is named—such is the intent of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: This is because a son, when addressing his father, uses his birth name; naming the son in the father's presence is the point of ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 是以桓公六年九月丁卯，子同生，《傳》曰：「舉以太子之禮。

translations.literal: Therefore in the sixth year of Duke Huan, on the day dingmao of the ninth month, Zitong was born; the Commentary says: "He was raised with the rites due the heir apparent."
translations.idiomatic: Hence in Duke Huan's sixth year, on the ninth month's dingmao day, Zitong was born, and the Commentary says, "He was raised with the rites due an heir apparent."

sentences.zh: 」杜預注云：「桓公子莊公也。

translations.literal: " Du Yu's note says: "He was Duke Huan's son, Duke Zhuang."
translations.idiomatic: " Du Yu's note explains, "This was Duke Huan's son, who became Duke Zhuang."

sentences.zh: 」十二公唯子同是嫡夫人之長子，備用太子之禮，故史書之於策。

translations.literal: " Of the twelve dukes only Zitong was the eldest son of the principal wife, fully provided with the rites of the heir apparent; therefore the historians recorded it in the chronicle.
translations.idiomatic: " Of the twelve dukes of Lu, only Zitong, eldest son of the principal wife, received the full rites of an heir apparent, which is why the annals record his name.

sentences.zh: 即位之日，尊成君而不名，《春秋》之義，聖人之微旨也。

translations.literal: On the day of accession he is honored as the completed lord and not named—such is the meaning of the Spring and Autumn, the subtle intent of the sage.
translations.idiomatic: From the day of accession he is honored as sovereign and left unnamed—this is the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals and the sage's subtle intent.

sentences.zh: 至如馬遷，周之太子並皆言名，漢之儲兩俱沒其諱，以尊漢卑周，臣子之意也。

translations.literal: As for Sima Qian, the heirs of Zhou are all given by name, while the heirs of Han all have their taboo names suppressed—honoring Han and demeaning Zhou: the intent of a subject.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Qian, for instance, names every Zhou heir apparent while suppressing the personal names of Han heirs—elevating Han and diminishing Zhou, as a loyal subject would.

sentences.zh: 竊謂雖立此理，恐非其義。

translations.literal: I venture to say that although this principle is set forth, I fear it is not correct in meaning.
translations.idiomatic: I would argue that although this principle is asserted, it is probably not sound.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why is that?

sentences.zh: 《春秋》、《禮記》，太子必書名，天王不言出。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn and the Record of Rites: the heir apparent must be named in writing; the King of Heaven does not speak of going forth.
translations.idiomatic: In the Spring and Autumn Annals and the Record of Rites, heirs apparent are always named, while the King of Heaven is never said to 'go forth.'

sentences.zh: 此仲尼之褒貶，皇王之稱謂，非當時與異代遂為優劣也。

translations.literal: This is Confucius's praise and blame, the titles of emperors and kings—not that the present age and a different age thereby become superior or inferior.
translations.idiomatic: These are Confucius's standards of praise and blame and the proper titles for sovereigns—not grounds for ranking one dynasty above another.

sentences.zh: 班固、范曄、陳壽、王隱、沈約參差不同，尊卑失序。

translations.literal: Ban Gu, Fan Ye, Chen Shou, Wang Yin, and Shen Yue differ unevenly, and the order of honor and baseness is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu, Fan Ye, Chen Shou, Wang Yin, and Shen Yue applied inconsistent rules, so the hierarchy of honor was lost.

sentences.zh: 至於魏收，諱儲君之名，書天子之字，過又甚焉。

translations.literal: As for Wei Shou, he tabooed the heir's name and wrote the Son of Heaven's style name—the excess was even greater.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou went further still, suppressing the heir's personal name while recording the emperor's style name.

sentences.zh: 今所撰史，諱皇帝名，書太子字，欲以尊君卑臣，依《春秋》之義也。

translations.literal: The history now compiled taboos the emperor's name and writes the heir's style name, wishing thereby to honor the ruler and demean the subject, following the meaning of the Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: In the history I now compile, the emperor's personal name is suppressed and the heir's style name is recorded, honoring the sovereign over the subject in accordance with the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 其二曰，五帝之聖，三代之英，積德累功，乃文乃武，賢聖相承，莫過周室，名器不及後稷，追諡止于三王，此即前代之茂實，後人之龜鏡也。

translations.literal: The second says: The sages of the Five Emperors, the heroes of the Three Dynasties, accumulating virtue and piling up merit, both cultured and martial, sage succeeding sage—none surpass the house of Zhou; titles and regalia did not reach Hou Ji, and posthumous titles stopped at the Three Kings. This is the abundant truth of former ages and a tortoise mirror for later men.
translations.idiomatic: The second principle: The Five Emperors were sages and the Three Dynasties produced heroes who amassed virtue and achievement in both civil and military arts, with sage succeeding sage—none surpassed the Zhou. Yet even Zhou did not grant full titles to Hou Ji, and posthumous honors stopped at the Three Kings. This is the model of antiquity and a mirror for posterity.

sentences.zh: 魏氏平文以前，部落之君長耳。

translations.literal: Before Emperor Pingwen of Wei, they were merely chieftains of tribal confederations.
translations.idiomatic: Before Emperor Pingwen, the Wei were merely tribal chieftains.

sentences.zh: 太祖遠追二十八帝，並極崇高，違堯舜憲章，越周公典禮。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor far pursued twenty-eight emperors, all to the utmost exaltation, violating the statutes of Yao and Shun and surpassing the canonical rites of the Duke of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor posthumously ennobled twenty-eight distant forebears to the highest rank, violating the precedents of Yao and Shun and exceeding the ritual canon of the Duke of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 但道武出自結繩，未師典誥，當須南、董直筆，裁而正之。

translations.literal: But Emperor Daowu came from the age of knotted cords and had not studied the canonical edicts; there should have been the straightforward brush of Nan and Dong to cut and correct it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daowu arose from an age before written law and had not mastered the classical edicts; this called for historians in the mold of Nan Shi and Dong Hu to set the record straight with an honest brush.

sentences.zh: 反更飾非，言是觀過，所謂決渤澥之水，復去堤防，襄陵之災，未可免也。

translations.literal: Instead they further adorned wrong as right, calling it observing faults—what is called breaching the waters of the Bohai Sea and again removing the dikes; the disaster of inundating the hills cannot be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: Instead the historians dressed up error as merit, calling it a charitable view of faults—like breaching the Bohai and tearing down the dikes again; a flood that submerges the hills cannot be avoided.

sentences.zh: 但力微天女所誕，靈異絕世，尊為始祖，得禮之宜。

translations.literal: Yet Li Wei was born of a heavenly maiden, miraculous and unmatched in the age; honoring him as Founding Ancestor accorded with ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wei, however, was said to be born of a heavenly maiden and was miraculous beyond his age; honoring him as Founding Ancestor was ritually appropriate.

sentences.zh: 平文、昭成雄據塞表，英風漸盛，圖南之業，基自此始。

translations.literal: Pingwen and Zhaocheng held the frontier regions heroically; their heroic wind gradually flourished, and the enterprise of turning south—its foundation began here.
translations.idiomatic: Emperors Pingwen and Zhaocheng held the northern frontier with growing power, and the ambition to march south took root with them.

sentences.zh: 長孫斤之亂也，兵交御坐，太子授命，昭成獲免。

translations.literal: In the turmoil of Changsun Jin, weapons clashed at the imperial seat; the heir transmitted the command, and Zhaocheng was spared.
translations.idiomatic: During the rebellion of Changsun Jin, fighting reached the imperial throne; the crown prince passed on the command, and Zhaocheng escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 道武此時，後緡方娠，宗廟復存，社稷有主，大功大孝，實在獻明。

translations.literal: At this time Daowu's consort Houfei was newly pregnant; the ancestral temple was preserved again, the altars of soil and grain had a lord; the great merit and great filial piety truly lay with Xianming.
translations.idiomatic: At that moment Daowu's consort was newly pregnant, the ancestral temple was preserved, and the realm again had a ruler; the great service and supreme filial act belonged truly to Xianming.

sentences.zh: 此之三世，稱諡可也。

translations.literal: For these three generations, posthumous titles may be applied.
translations.idiomatic: These three generations may properly receive posthumous titles.

sentences.zh: 自茲以外，未之敢聞。

translations.literal: Beyond this, I have not dared to hear of it.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond them I would not venture to go.

sentences.zh: 其三曰，臣以為南巢桀亡，牧野紂滅，斬以黃鉞，懸首白旗，幽王死於驪山，厲王出奔於彘，未嘗隱諱，直筆書之，欲以勸善懲惡，貽誡將來者也。

translations.literal: The third says: Your subject holds that Jie perished at Nan-chao, Zhou perished at Muye—they were beheaded with the yellow battle-axe and their heads hung on white banners; King You died at Mount Li, King Li fled to Zhi—never were these concealed; the straightforward brush wrote them, wishing thereby to encourage good and punish evil and leave admonition for the future.
translations.idiomatic: The third principle: When Jie fell at Nan-chao and Zhou at Muye they were struck down with the yellow axe and their heads displayed on white banners; when King You died at Mount Li and King Li fled to Zhi, the annalists did not conceal these facts but wrote them plainly to encourage virtue, punish wickedness, and warn posterity.

sentences.zh: 而太武、獻文並皆非命，前史立紀，不異天年，言論之間，頗露首尾。

translations.literal: Yet Emperor Taiwu and Emperor Xianwen both died by violence; the former history made annals for them no different from natural years, and between the lines of discourse the beginning and end were rather exposed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Emperors Taiwu and Xianwen both died by violence, while the earlier history treated their reigns like natural deaths, though its wording still betrayed the truth at both ends.

sentences.zh: 殺主害君，莫知名姓，逆臣賊子，何所懼哉！

translations.literal: Those who killed their lords and harmed their rulers—no name or surname is known; rebellious ministers and wicked sons—what have they to fear!
translations.idiomatic: When regicides go unnamed, what restraint is left for traitors and parricides?

sentences.zh: 君子之過，如日月之食，圓首方足，孰不瞻仰？

translations.literal: The faults of the noble man are like eclipses of sun and moon; round-headed and square-footed—all who do not look up in reverence?
translations.idiomatic: A nobleman's faults are like eclipses of the sun and moon—everyone under heaven sees them plainly.

sentences.zh: 況復兵交御坐，矢及王屋，而可隱沒者乎！

translations.literal: How much more when weapons clashed at the imperial seat and arrows reached the royal chamber—how could these be concealed!
translations.idiomatic: How much less can one conceal fighting at the throne itself and arrows striking the royal hall!

sentences.zh: 今所撰史，分明直書，不敢回避。

translations.literal: The history now compiled writes clearly and directly, not daring to evade.
translations.idiomatic: In the history I now compile I write plainly and directly, without evasion.

sentences.zh: 且隱、桓之死，閔、昭殺逐，丘明據實敘於經下，況復懸隔異代而致依違哉！

translations.literal: Moreover the deaths of Yin and Huan, the killing and expulsion of Min and Zhao—Qiu Ming narrated them according to fact beneath the classic; how much more when separated by distant ages to become evasive!
translations.idiomatic: When Yin and Huan died and Min and Zhao were killed and driven out, Qiu Ming recorded the facts beneath the classic lines; how much less should one hedge when the ages are far apart!

sentences.zh: 其四曰，周道陵遲，不勝其敝，楚子親問九鼎，吳人來征百牢，無君之心，實彰行路，夫子刊經，皆書曰卒。

translations.literal: The fourth says: The Way of Zhou declined and could not bear its decay; the lord of Chu in person asked about the Nine Cauldrons, men of Wu came to levy the hundred enclosures—the heart without a lord was truly manifest on the road; the Master edited the classic and all wrote "died."
translations.idiomatic: The fourth principle: As the Zhou Way declined beyond repair, the lord of Chu inquired after the Nine Cauldrons and men of Wu came to demand the hundred enclosures of sacrificial meat—their disloyalty was plain to every traveler, and when the Master edited the classics he recorded their ends simply as "died."

sentences.zh: 自晉德不競，宇宙分崩，或帝或王，各自署置。

translations.literal: From the time Jin's virtue could not contend, the cosmos split apart; some called themselves emperors, some kings, each establishing titles for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jin's virtue failed, the realm shattered, and men styled themselves emperor or king as they pleased.

sentences.zh: 當其生日，聘使往來，略如敵國，及其終也，書之日死，便同庶人。

translations.literal: While they lived, envoys came and went much like between enemy states; when they ended, the annals wrote "died on such-and-such a day," equating them with commoners.
translations.idiomatic: During their lives envoys exchanged visits almost as between rival states, yet at their deaths the annals wrote "died on such-and-such a day," reducing them to commoners.

sentences.zh: 存沒頓殊，能無懷愧！

translations.literal: Alive and dead so abruptly different—how could one not feel shame!
translations.idiomatic: Such a gulf between life and death—how could one not blush at the inconsistency!

sentences.zh: 今所撰史，諸國凡處華夏之地者，皆書曰卒，同之吳、楚。

translations.literal: The history now compiled: for all states situated in the lands of Huaxia, all write "died," treating them the same as Wu and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: In the history I now compile, every state within the Central Plains is recorded as having "died," on the same terms as Wu and Chu.

sentences.zh: 其五曰，壺遂發問，馬遷答之，義已盡矣。

translations.literal: The fifth says: Hu Sui raised the question and Sima Qian answered it—the meaning was already complete.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth principle: When Hu Sui posed the question and Sima Qian answered it, the matter was already settled.

sentences.zh: 後之述者，仍未領悟。

translations.literal: Later compilers still have not understood.
translations.idiomatic: Later historians still failed to grasp the point.

sentences.zh: 董仲舒、司馬遷之意，本雲《尚書》者，隆平之典，《春秋》者，撥亂之法，興衰理異，製作亦殊。

translations.literal: The intent of Dong Zhongshu and Sima Qian originally said: the Documents are the canon of abundant peace; the Spring and Autumn is the law for setting chaos aright; rise and fall follow different principles, and their composition is also distinct.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhongshu and Sima Qian held that the Documents record an age of peace and plenty, while the Spring and Autumn provides the method for restoring order in chaos; rise and decline follow different principles, and the two works were composed for different purposes.

sentences.zh: 治定則直敘欽明，世亂則辭兼顯晦，分路命家，不相依放。

translations.literal: When order is settled one narrates directly the reverent clarity; when the age is chaotic the diction combines manifest and hidden; they part ways and appoint their houses, not relying on one another.
translations.idiomatic: When order is secure one narrates plainly the virtues of the sage-kings; when the age is chaotic the language mixes clarity and concealment; each tradition follows its own path and does not borrow from the other.

sentences.zh: 故云「周道廢，《春秋》作焉，堯、舜盛，《尚書》載之」是也。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: "When the Way of Zhou was abandoned, the Spring and Autumn was made; when Yao and Shun flourished, the Documents recorded them"—such is the case.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying: "When the Zhou Way fell into ruin, the Spring and Autumn was composed; when Yao and Shun flourished, the Documents recorded them."

sentences.zh: 「漢興以來，改正朔，易服色，臣力誦聖德，仍不能盡，餘所謂述故事，而君比之《春秋》，謬哉」。

translations.literal: "Since Han arose, the calendar has been corrected and ceremonial colors changed; your subject strives to recite the sage's virtue yet still cannot exhaust it; what I call narrating past affairs—yet you compare it to the Spring and Autumn: how mistaken!"
translations.idiomatic: "Since Han arose, calendars and ceremonial colors have been revised; I strive to proclaim the sage emperor's virtue yet cannot exhaust it. What I call recounting past events you compare to the Spring and Autumn—that is a mistake."

sentences.zh: 然則紀傳之體出自《尚書》，不學《春秋》，明矣。

translations.literal: Thus the annal-biography form derives from the Documents and does not learn from the Spring and Autumn—it is clear.
translations.idiomatic: It is clear, then, that the annal-and-biography format derives from the Documents, not from the Spring and Autumn.

sentences.zh: 而范曄云：「《春秋》者，文既總略，好失事形，今之擬作，所以為短。

translations.literal: Yet Fan Ye said: "The Spring and Autumn: its text is already summary and general, tending to lose the shape of events; imitating it in present composition is therefore a shortcoming."
translations.idiomatic: Yet Fan Ye wrote, "The Spring and Autumn is so summary in style that it often loses the concrete shape of events; modeling present work on it is therefore a defect."

sentences.zh: 紀傳者，史、班之所變也，網羅一代，事義周悉，適之後學，此焉為優，故繼而述之。

translations.literal: Annal-biography is what Shi and Ban transformed; it nets a whole generation, events and meanings complete and thorough, suited to later students—herein lies its superiority; therefore I continue and narrate it.
translations.idiomatic: "Annal-biography is the form developed by Sima Qian and Ban Gu; it encompasses a whole age with thorough coverage of events and meanings, and suits later students better, which is why I follow that model."

sentences.zh: 」觀曄此言，豈直非聖人之無法，又失馬遷之意旨。

translations.literal: " Considering Ye's words, is it only that he lacks the sage's method? He also misses the intent of Sima Qian.
translations.idiomatic: " Reading Fan Ye's words, he not only abandons the sage's method but also misses Sima Qian's intent entirely.

sentences.zh: 孫盛自謂鑽仰具體而放之。

translations.literal: Sun Sheng claimed for himself that he bored in and looked up to the full form and then emulated it.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng claimed to have studied the complete model closely and then adapted it.

sentences.zh: 魏收云：「魯史既修，達者貽則，子長自拘紀傳，不存師表，蓋泉源所由，地非企及。

translations.literal: Wei Shou said: "Once the Lu chronicle was completed, the accomplished left a standard; Zichang confined himself to annal-biography and did not preserve the master's model—surely the spring's source from which it arose is ground one cannot hope to reach."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou wrote, "After the Lu chronicle was completed, the wise left a standard for posterity; Sima Qian confined himself to annal-biography and did not preserve the master's model—the spring from which he drew lies on ground one cannot hope to reach."

sentences.zh: 」雖復遜辭畏聖，亦未思紀傳所由來也。

translations.literal: " Though again using modest words in awe of the sage, he also had not considered whence annal-biography arose.
translations.idiomatic: " Even in his modest deference to the sage, he never considered where annal-biography actually came from.

sentences.zh: 澹又以為司馬遷創立紀傳以來，述者非一，人無善惡，皆為立論。

translations.literal: Dan also held that since Sima Qian established annal-biography, narrators have not been few; whether persons were good or evil, all received discursive essays.
translations.idiomatic: Dan also held that since Sima Qian created the annal-biography format, countless historians have written evaluative essays for figures good and bad alike.

sentences.zh: 計在身行跡，具在正書，事既無奇，不足懲勸。

translations.literal: Considering that conduct and traces of the person are fully in the main text, events being without marvel, they are insufficient to warn and encourage.
translations.idiomatic: Since a person's conduct is already fully recorded in the main text, and the facts are nothing out of the ordinary, such essays add little by way of moral instruction.

sentences.zh: 再述乍同銘頌，重敘唯覺繁文。

translations.literal: To narrate again is suddenly like an inscription or eulogy; to recount repeatedly one only feels redundant text.
translations.idiomatic: A second account reads like an inscription or eulogy, and repetition only makes the prose feel bloated.

sentences.zh: 案丘明亞聖之才，發揚聖旨，言「君子曰」者，無非甚泰，其間尋常，直書而已。

translations.literal: Considering Qiu Ming's talent next to the sage, in expounding the sage's intent, where it says "the noble man says," nothing is not greatly elevated; in between, what is ordinary is simply written directly.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Ming, second only to the sage in talent, expounded the sage's intent; when he wrote "the noble man says," the judgment was always weighty, while ordinary matters he recorded plainly.

sentences.zh: 今所撰史，竊有慕焉，可為勸戒者，論其得失，其無損益者，所不論也。

translations.literal: The history now compiled, I privately have admiration for this: where it can serve as admonition, discuss its gains and losses; what has no benefit or harm, I do not discuss.
translations.idiomatic: In the history I now compile I follow this model: where moral instruction is possible, I discuss a person's merits and faults; where nothing is gained or lost, I pass over the matter.

sentences.zh: 澹所著《魏書》，甚簡要，大矯收、繪之失。

translations.literal: Dan's History of Wei that he authored was very concise and brief, greatly correcting the errors of Shou and Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Dan's History of Wei was notably concise and corrected most of the faults of Wei Shou and Ping Hui.

sentences.zh: 上覽而善之。

translations.literal: The emperor read it and approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read it and was pleased.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒，時年六十五。

translations.literal: Before long he died, at age sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward, at the age of sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 有《文集》三十卷行於世。

translations.literal: He had Collected Works in thirty scrolls circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works in thirty scrolls circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 子信言，頗知名。

translations.literal: His son Xinyan was rather well known.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xinyan achieved considerable renown.

sentences.zh: 澹弟彥玄，有文學，歷揚州總管府記室、洧州司馬。

translations.literal: Dan's younger brother Yanxuan had literary learning and successively served as Recorder of the Yangzhou Regional Command headquarters and Military Administrator of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Dan's younger brother Yanxuan was a man of letters who served as Recorder on the Yangzhou headquarters staff and later as Military Administrator of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 有子滿行。

translations.literal: He had a son Manxing.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son named Manxing.

sentences.zh: 陸爽陸爽，字開明，魏郡臨漳人也。

translations.literal: Lu Shuang, styled Kaiming, was a native of Linzhang in Wei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shuang, whose style name was Kaiming, came from Linzhang in Wei commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖順宗，魏南青州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shunzong was Governor of Southern Qingzhou under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shunzong had served Wei as Governor of Southern Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 父概之，齊霍州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Gaizhi was Governor of Huozhou under Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gaizhi had served Qi as Governor of Huozhou.

sentences.zh: 爽少聰敏，年九歲就學，日誦二千餘言。

translations.literal: Shuang from youth was clever; at nine he began study and recited more than two thousand words daily.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Shuang was quick-witted; at nine he took up his studies and recited more than two thousand characters a day.

sentences.zh: 齊尚書僕射楊遵彥見而異之，曰：「陸氏代有人焉。

translations.literal: Yang Zunyan, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing in Qi, saw him and marveled, saying: "Generation after generation the Lu house produces men."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zunyan, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing under Qi, saw him and exclaimed, "The Lu clan has produced worthy men in every generation."

sentences.zh: 」年十七，齊司州牧、清河王嶽召為主簿。

translations.literal: " At seventeen, Yue, Prince of Qinghe and Regional Governor of Sizhou in Qi, summoned him as Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen he was summoned by Yue, Prince of Qinghe and Regional Governor of Sizhou, and appointed Chief Clerk on his staff.

sentences.zh: 擢殿中侍御史，俄兼治書，累轉中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Palace Attendant Censor, soon also served concurrently as Drafting Secretary, and through successive transfers became Secretariat Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Palace Attendant Censor, soon held concurrent duty as Drafting Secretary, and rose through successive posts to Secretariat Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 及齊滅，周武帝聞其名，與陽休之、袁叔德等十餘人俱征入關。

translations.literal: When Qi fell, Emperor Wu of Zhou heard his name and, together with Yang Xiuzhi, Yuan Shude, and more than ten others, summoned them all to enter the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi fell, Emperor Wu of Zhou summoned him, together with Yang Xiuzhi, Yuan Shude, and more than ten others, to enter the Pass.

sentences.zh: 諸人多將輜重，爽獨載書數千卷。

translations.literal: Most of the others brought heavy baggage; Shuang alone loaded several thousand scrolls of books.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the others brought wagonloads of goods, but Shuang alone carried several thousand scrolls of books.

sentences.zh: 至長安，授宣納上士。

translations.literal: On reaching Chang'an he was appointed Xuan'na Upper Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Chang'an he was appointed Xuan'na Upper Grandee.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，轉太子內直監，尋遷太子洗馬。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication he was transferred to Director of Inner Attendants to the Heir Apparent, and soon promoted to Palace Stud Groom to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne he was made Director of Inner Attendants to the Heir Apparent and soon promoted to Palace Stud Groom to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 與左庶子宇文愷等撰《東宮典記》七十卷。

translations.literal: Together with Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent Yuwen Kai and others, he compiled the Eastern Palace Standard Records in seventy scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent Yuwen Kai and others, he compiled the Eastern Palace Standard Records in seventy scrolls.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以其博學有口辯，陳人至境，常令迎勞。

translations.literal: Because the court regarded him as broadly learned and eloquent, whenever Chen envoys reached the border he was regularly ordered to welcome and entertain them.
translations.idiomatic: Because the court regarded him as broadly learned and gifted in debate, whenever Chen envoys arrived at the frontier he was regularly sent to welcome and entertain them.

sentences.zh: 開皇十一年，卒官，時年五十三，贈上儀同、宣州刺史，賜帛百匹。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Kaihuang he died in office at age fifty-three; posthumously granted Senior Commissioner with Protocol Equal to the Three Dukes and Governor of Xuanzhou, with one hundred bolts of silk awarded.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang 11 he died in office at fifty-three; posthumously he was granted Senior Commissioner with Protocol Equal to the Three Dukes and Governor of Xuanzhou, with one hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 子法言，敏學有家風，釋褐承奉郎。

translations.literal: His son Fayán was quick in learning and inherited the family tradition; upon first taking office he became Gentleman of the Palace Reception.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fayán was quick in learning and carried on the family tradition; upon entering office he was appointed Gentleman of the Palace Reception.

sentences.zh: 初，爽之為洗馬，嘗奏高祖云：「皇太子諸子未有嘉名，請依《春秋》之義，更立名字。

translations.literal: Earlier, while Shuang was Palace Stud Groom, he once memorialized Gaozu: "The crown prince's sons still lack fine names; I ask that new names be established according to the principles of the Spring and Autumn Annals."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while serving as Palace Stud Groom, Shuang memorialized Gaozu: "The crown prince's sons still have no auspicious names; I ask that new names be established according to the principles of the Spring and Autumn Annals."

sentences.zh: 」上從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor followed his request.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 及太子廢，上追怒爽云：「我孫制名，甯不自解？

translations.literal: When the crown prince was deposed, the emperor later turned his anger on Shuang and said: "When I name my grandsons, could I not understand that myself?
translations.idiomatic: After the crown prince was deposed, the emperor turned on Shuang in anger and said, "When I name my grandsons, could I not decide that for myself?

sentences.zh: 陸爽乃爾多事！

translations.literal: Lu Shuang was meddling to this degree!
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shuang had meddled far too much!

sentences.zh: 扇惑於勇，亦由此人。

translations.literal: That he swayed Yong also came from this man.
translations.idiomatic: That Yong was led astray also stemmed from this man.

sentences.zh: 其身雖故，子孫並宜屏黜，終身不齒。

translations.literal: Though he himself is dead, his descendants should all be removed and ostracized, never counted among their peers for life.
translations.idiomatic: Though he himself was already dead, his descendants should all be cast out and banished from office, never to be received among their peers for life.

sentences.zh: 」法言竟坐除名。

translations.literal: " Fayán in the end was punished by having his name struck from the registers.
translations.idiomatic: Fayán was ultimately removed from the official rolls.

sentences.zh: 侯白爽同郡侯白，字君素，好學有捷才，性滑稽，尤辯俊。

translations.literal: Hou Bai of the same commandery as Shuang, styled Junsu, loved learning and had quick talent; by nature comical, he especially excelled in eloquence and wit.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Bai, styled Junsu, came from the same commandery as Shuang. He loved learning and possessed quick talent; by nature he was comical and excelled in eloquence and wit.

sentences.zh: 舉秀才，為儒林郎。

translations.literal: He passed the provincial examination and became Erudite of the Forest of Classics.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as Presented Scholar, he was appointed Erudite of the Forest of Classics.

sentences.zh: 通侻不恃威儀，好為誹諧雜說，人多愛狎之，所在之處，觀者如市。

translations.literal: Easygoing and unrestrained, he did not rely on formal dignity; he loved satirical and humorous talk, and crowds gathered wherever he went like a market.
translations.idiomatic: Unrestrained in manner, he cared little for formal dignity and loved satirical and humorous pieces; crowds gathered wherever he appeared as thick as at a market.

sentences.zh: 楊素甚狎之。

translations.literal: Yang Su was very intimate with him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su was especially fond of him.

sentences.zh: 素嘗與牛弘退朝，白謂素曰：「日之夕矣。

translations.literal: Su once withdrew from court with Niu Hong, and Bai said to Su: "The sun is setting."
translations.idiomatic: Once, as Su was leaving court with Niu Hong, Bai said to him, "The sun is setting."

sentences.zh: 」素大笑曰：「以我為牛羊下來邪？

translations.literal: " Su laughed loudly and said: "Do you take me for cattle and sheep coming down in the evening?
translations.idiomatic: Su laughed aloud and said, "Do you take me for cattle and sheep coming down at dusk?

sentences.zh: 」高祖聞其名，召與語，甚悅之，令于秘書修國史。

translations.literal: " Gaozu heard his name, summoned him to converse, was greatly pleased, and ordered him to compile the national history in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu heard his name, summoned him for an audience, was greatly pleased, and ordered him to work on the national history in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 每將擢之，高祖輒曰：「侯白不勝官」而止。

translations.literal: Whenever they were about to promote him, Gaozu would say "Hou Bai cannot bear office" and stop.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a promotion was proposed, Gaozu would say, "Hou Bai is not fit for office," and the matter would go no further.

sentences.zh: 後給五品食，月餘而死，時人傷其薄命。

translations.literal: Later he was granted fifth-rank stipend; after a little more than a month he died, and people grieved over his short life.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was granted the stipend of a fifth-rank official; a little more than a month afterward he died, and contemporaries mourned his ill-fated life.

sentences.zh: 著《旌異記》十五卷，行於世。

translations.literal: He wrote Records of Marvels and Anomalies in fifteen scrolls, circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Records of Marvels and Anomalies in fifteen scrolls, which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 杜臺卿杜臺卿，字少山，博陵曲陽人也。

translations.literal: Du Taiqing, styled Shaoshan, was a native of Quyang in Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Du Taiqing, whose style name was Shaoshan, came from Quyang in Boling commandery.

sentences.zh: 父弼，齊衛尉卿。

translations.literal: His father Bi was Minister of the Guards in Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bi had served Qi as Minister of the Guards.

sentences.zh: 臺卿少好學，博覽書記，解屬文。

translations.literal: Taiqing from youth loved learning, read widely in books and records, and was skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Taiqing loved learning, read widely in books and records, and was accomplished at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 仕齊奉朝請，歷司空西閤祭酒、司徒戶曹、著作郎、中書黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He served Qi as Attendant at Court and passed through Libationer of the Western Pavilion under the Minister of Works, staff of the Household Bureau, Drafting Gentleman, and Secretariat Yellow Gate Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qi he served as Attendant at Court and held the posts of Libationer of the Western Pavilion, staff member in the Household Bureau, Drafting Gentleman, and Secretariat Yellow Gate Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 性儒素，每以雅道自居。

translations.literal: By nature Confucian and plain, he always took refined principles as his standard.
translations.idiomatic: Plain and upright by nature, he always held himself to the standards of refined conduct.

sentences.zh: 及周武帝平齊，歸於鄉里，以《禮記》、《春秋》講授子弟。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou pacified Qi, he returned home and lectured on the Record of Rites and the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu of Zhou conquered Qi, he returned home and lectured on the Record of Rites and the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，被征入朝。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang he was summoned to court.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Kaihuang era he was summoned to court.

sentences.zh: 臺卿嘗采《月令》，觸類而廣之，為書名《玉燭寶典》十二卷。

translations.literal: Taiqing drew on the Monthly Ordinances and, extending by analogous categories, made the Jade Candle Precious Canon in twelve scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Taiqing drew on the Monthly Ordinances and, extending the material by analogous categories, produced the Jade Candle Precious Canon in twelve scrolls.

sentences.zh: 至是奏之，賜絹二百匹。

translations.literal: At this time he submitted it and was granted two hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted it to the throne and was rewarded with two hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 臺卿患聾，不堪吏職，請修國史。

translations.literal: Taiqing suffered deafness and could not bear administrative duty, so he requested to compile the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Afflicted with deafness, Taiqing could not manage administrative duties and asked instead to compile the national history.

sentences.zh: 上許之，拜著作郎。

translations.literal: The emperor approved and appointed him Drafting Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted his request and appointed him Drafting Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 十四年，上表請致仕，敕以本官還第。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he submitted a memorial requesting retirement; an edict ordered him home while retaining his rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he requested retirement; an edict permitted him to return home while retaining his former rank.

sentences.zh: 數載，終於家。

translations.literal: After several years he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he died at home.

sentences.zh: 有集十五卷，撰《齊記》二十卷，並行於世。

translations.literal: He left collected writings in fifteen scrolls and compiled Records of Qi in twenty scrolls; both circulated.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected writings in fifteen scrolls and compiled Records of Qi in twenty scrolls; both circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 無子。

translations.literal: He had no son.
translations.idiomatic: He had no son.

sentences.zh: 有兄蕤，學業不如臺卿，而幹局過之。

translations.literal: He had an elder brother Rui, whose learning did not match Taiqing's but whose practical capacity surpassed his.
translations.idiomatic: He had an elder brother Rui, whose scholarship did not equal Taiqing's but whose practical capacity for affairs surpassed his.

sentences.zh: 仕至開州刺史。

translations.literal: In office he rose to Prefect of Kaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In office he rose to Prefect of Kaizhou.

sentences.zh: 子公贍，少好學，有家風，卒於安陽令。

translations.literal: His son Gongshan from youth loved learning and inherited the family tradition; he died as Magistrate of Anyang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gongshan loved learning from youth and carried on the family tradition; he died while serving as Magistrate of Anyang.

sentences.zh: 公贍子之松，大業中，為起居舍人。

translations.literal: Gongshan's son Zhison, in the Daye era, served as Attendant of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Gongshan's son Zhison served as Attendant of the Palace during the Daye era.

sentences.zh: 辛德源辛德源，字孝基，隴西狄道人也。

translations.literal: Xin Deyuan, styled Xiaoji, was a native of Didao in Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Deyuan, whose style name was Xiaoji, came from Didao in Longxi commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖穆，魏平原太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Mu was Prefect of Pingyuan in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Mu had served Wei as Prefect of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 父子馥，尚書右丞。

translations.literal: His father Zifu was Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zifu served as Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 德源沉靜好學，年十四，解屬文。

translations.literal: Deyuan was calm and loved learning; at fourteen he was skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Calm and reserved, Deyuan loved learning and at fourteen was accomplished at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 及長，博覽書記，少有重名。

translations.literal: When grown he read widely and from youth had a great reputation.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he read widely in books and records and early on acquired a considerable reputation.

sentences.zh: 齊尚書僕射楊遵彥、殿中尚書辛術皆一時名士，見德源，並虛襟禮敬，因同薦之于文宣帝。

translations.literal: Yang Zunyan and Xin Shu, celebrated men of Qi, received Deyuan with open courtesy and together recommended him to Emperor Wenxuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zunyan, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and Xin Shu, Director within the Palace, were celebrated men of their age; on meeting Deyuan they received him with open courtesy and together recommended him to Emperor Wenxuan.

sentences.zh: 起家奉朝請，後為兼員外散騎侍郎，聘梁使副。

translations.literal: He first served as Attendant at Court, later as Supernumerary Vice Director of the Cavalry-in-Attendance and deputy envoy to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He began as Attendant at Court, later served as Supernumerary Vice Director of the Cavalry-in-Attendance and went to Liang as deputy envoy.

sentences.zh: 後曆馮翊、華山二王記室。

translations.literal: Later he served as Recorder on the staffs of the Princes of Fenyang and Huashan.
translations.idiomatic: He later served in turn as Recorder on the staffs of the Princes of Fenyang and Huashan.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎劉逖上表薦德源曰：「弱齡好古，晚節逾厲，枕藉六經，漁獵百氏。

translations.literal: Liu Ti, Vice Director of the Secretariat, recommended Deyuan: "From youth he loved antiquity; in later years he grew stricter; he reclines upon the Six Classics and hunts through the hundred schools."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ti, Vice Director of the Secretariat, recommended Deyuan: "From youth he loved antiquity, and in later life he grew ever more rigorous; he rests upon the Six Classics and ranges through the writings of the hundred schools."

sentences.zh: 文章綺豔，體調清華，恭慎表於閨門，謙捴著於朋執。

translations.literal: His writings are ornate, his tone refined; reverence shows in his household and modesty among friends.
translations.idiomatic: His writings are rich and brilliant, his literary tone clear and refined; reverence and caution mark his household, and modesty is evident among his friends.

sentences.zh: 實後進之辭人，當今之雅器。

translations.literal: He is truly a literary talent of the younger generation and a refined vessel of the age.
translations.idiomatic: He is truly a literary talent among the rising generation and a refined man of the present age.

sentences.zh: 必能效節一官，騁足千里。

translations.literal: He is sure to devote his integrity to one office and run a thousand li at a stretch.
translations.idiomatic: He is sure to serve one office with full devotion and prove capable of far-reaching achievement.

sentences.zh: 」由是除員外散騎侍郎，累遷比部郎中，復兼通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: " Thereupon appointed Vice Director of the Cavalry-in-Attendance, promoted to Director in the Ministry of Justice, and again Regular Attendant of Direct Communication and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: On this basis he was appointed Vice Director of the Cavalry-in-Attendance, rose to Director in the Ministry of Justice, and again served concurrently as Regular Attendant of Direct Communication and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 聘于陳，及還，待詔文林館，除尚書考功郎中，轉中書舍人。

translations.literal: Sent to Chen; on return kept at the Wenlin Hall, appointed Director of Evaluations, then Drafting Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: After serving as envoy to Chen, he was retained at the Wenlin Hall, appointed Director of Evaluations in the Ministry of Personnel, and then transferred to Drafting Secretary.

sentences.zh: 及齊滅，仕周為宣納上士。

translations.literal: When Qi fell he served Zhou as Xuan'na Upper Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi fell, he served Northern Zhou as Xuan'na Upper Grandee.

sentences.zh: 因取急詣相州，會尉迥作亂，以為中郎。

translations.literal: On urgent leave to Xiangzhou he encountered Yu Jiong's rebellion and was made Middle Commander.
translations.idiomatic: While on urgent leave on his way to Xiangzhou, he encountered Yu Jiong's rebellion and was appointed Middle Commander under him.

sentences.zh: 德源辭不獲免，遂亡去。

translations.literal: Deyuan declined but could not escape; he fled.
translations.idiomatic: Deyuan refused but could not avoid the appointment, and so fled.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，不得調者久之，隱于林慮山，鬱鬱不得志，著《幽居賦》以自寄，文多不載。

translations.literal: When Gaozu took the throne he long went without appointment; he hid on Mount Linlü and wrote the Secluded Living Rhapsody—most of the text is not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu took the throne he long remained without appointment; he withdrew to Mount Linlü, depressed and unfulfilled, and wrote the Secluded Living Rhapsody—most of the text is not recorded here.

sentences.zh: 德源素與武陽太守盧思道友善，時相往來。

translations.literal: Deyuan was friendly with Lu Sidao, Prefect of Wuyang, and they frequently visited one another.
translations.idiomatic: Deyuan had long been close friends with Lu Sidao, Prefect of Wuyang, and they frequently visited one another.

sentences.zh: 魏州刺史崔彥武奏德源潛為交結，恐其有奸計。

translations.literal: Cui Yanwu, Prefect of Weizhou, memorialized that Deyuan secretly maintained connections and might harbor treacherous designs.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yanwu, Prefect of Weizhou, memorialized that Deyuan was secretly maintaining illicit contacts and might harbor treacherous designs.

sentences.zh: 由是謫令從軍討南寧，歲餘而還。

translations.literal: On this account he was demoted and ordered to join the army against Nanning; after more than a year he returned.
translations.idiomatic: On this account he was demoted and ordered to join the army on the Nanning campaign; he returned after more than a year.

sentences.zh: 秘書監牛弘以德源才學顯著，奏與著作郎王劭同修國史。

translations.literal: Niu Hong, Director of the Secretariat, memorialized that Deyuan compile the national history with Wang Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Because Deyuan's talent and learning were outstanding, Director of the Secretariat Niu Hong memorialized that he compile the national history together with Drafting Gentleman Wang Shao.

sentences.zh: 德源每於務隙撰《集注春秋三傳》三十卷，注揚子《法言》二十三卷。

translations.literal: In spare moments he wrote Collected Commentaries on the Three Commentaries on the Spring and Autumn in thirty scrolls and annotated Yang Xiong's Exemplary Words in twenty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In spare moments from his duties Deyuan wrote Collected Commentaries on the Three Commentaries on the Spring and Autumn in thirty scrolls and annotated Yang Xiong's Exemplary Words in twenty-three scrolls.

sentences.zh: 蜀王秀聞其名而引之，居數歲，奏以為掾。

translations.literal: Prince Xiu of Shu heard his name and summoned him; after several years memorialized him as staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiu of Shu, having heard his reputation, summoned him; after several years he memorialized that Deyuan be appointed a staff officer.

sentences.zh: 後轉諮議參軍，卒官。

translations.literal: Later transferred to Advisory Assistant and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to Advisory Assistant and died in office.

sentences.zh: 有集二十卷，又撰《政訓》、《內訓》各二十卷。

translations.literal: He left collected writings in twenty scrolls and wrote Political Instruction and Inner Instruction, each in twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected writings in twenty scrolls and also wrote Political Instruction and Inner Instruction, each in twenty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 有子素臣、正臣，並學涉有文義。

translations.literal: He had sons Suchén and Zhèngchén, both broadly learned and accomplished in letters.
translations.idiomatic: He had sons Suchén and Zhèngchén, both broadly learned and accomplished in letters.

sentences.zh: 柳䛒柳䛒，字顧言，本河東人也，永嘉之亂，徙家襄陽。

translations.literal: Liu Bian, styled Guyán, was originally from Hedong; in the Yongjia turmoil his family moved to Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bian, whose style name was Guyán, was originally from Hedong; during the upheavals of the Yongjia era his family moved to Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 祖惔，梁侍中。

translations.literal: His grandfather Tan was Attendant-in-ordinary of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Tan had served Liang as Attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 父暉，都官尚書。

translations.literal: His father Hui was Director of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hui served as Director of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 抃少聰敏，解屬文，好讀書，所覽將萬卷。

translations.literal: Bian from youth was clever, skilled at composition, loved reading, and had read nearly ten thousand scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Bian was quick-witted and skilled at literary composition; he loved reading and had perused nearly ten thousand scrolls.

sentences.zh: 仕梁，釋褐著作佐郎。

translations.literal: He served Liang and upon first taking office became Assistant Drafting Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang he entered office as Assistant Drafting Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 後蕭詧據荊州，以為侍中，領國子祭酒、吏部尚書。

translations.literal: When Xiao Cha held Jingzhou, Bian was made Attendant-in-ordinary, Chancellor of the Imperial Academy, and Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Cha held Jingzhou, he was made Attendant-in-ordinary and concurrently Chancellor of the Imperial Academy and Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 及梁國廢，拜開府、通直散騎常侍，尋遷內史侍郎。

translations.literal: When the Liang state was abolished, he was appointed General of the Opening Office and Regular Attendant of Direct Communication and Cavalry, soon Vice Director of the Inner Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang state was abolished, he was appointed General of the Opening Office and Regular Attendant of Direct Communication and Cavalry, and soon promoted to Vice Director of the Inner Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 以無吏幹去職，轉晉王諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Lacking administrative capacity he left that office and was transferred to Advisory Assistant to the Prince of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Lacking administrative capacity, he left that post and was transferred to Advisory Assistant on the staff of the Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 王好文雅，招引才學之士諸葛潁、虞世南、王胄、朱瑒等百餘人以充學士，而抃為之冠。

translations.literal: The prince loved refined letters and gathered more than a hundred scholars—Zhuge Ying, Yu Shinan, Wang Zhou, Zhu Yang, and others—with Bian foremost.
translations.idiomatic: The prince loved refined letters and gathered more than a hundred men of talent and learning—among them Zhuge Ying, Yu Shinan, Wang Zhou, and Zhu Yang—with Bian foremost among them.

sentences.zh: 王以師友處之，每有文什，必令其潤色，然後示人。

translations.literal: The prince treated him as teacher and friend; whenever he had a literary piece he had Bian polish it before showing it to others.
translations.idiomatic: The prince treated him as teacher and friend; whenever he wrote something, he always had Bian revise it before showing it to others.

sentences.zh: 嘗朝京師還，作《歸籓賦》，命抃為序，詞甚典麗。

translations.literal: Returning from the capital he wrote the Return to the Fief Rhapsody and ordered Bian to compose its preface; the language was very classical and beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: Once, on returning from an audience in the capital, he wrote the Return to the Fief Rhapsody and ordered Bian to compose its preface; the language was exceptionally classical and elegant.

sentences.zh: 初，王屬文，為庾信體，及見抃已後，文體遂變。

translations.literal: At first the prince wrote in the style of Yu Xin; after he met Bian his literary style changed.
translations.idiomatic: At first the prince wrote in the style of Yu Xin; after he came to know Bian, his literary style changed.

sentences.zh: 仁壽初，引抃為東宮學士，加通直散騎常侍，檢校洗馬，甚見親待。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Renshou he summoned Bian as Eastern Palace scholar, added Regular Attendant of Direct Communication and Cavalry, and made him Supervisory Palace Stud Groom; he was greatly favored.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Renshou era he summoned Bian as an Eastern Palace scholar, granted him the additional title Regular Attendant of Direct Communication and Cavalry, and appointed him Supervisory Palace Stud Groom; he was greatly favored and treated with special intimacy.

sentences.zh: 每召入臥內，與之宴謔。

translations.literal: Each time he summoned him into the inner sleeping chamber and feasted and jested with him.
translations.idiomatic: He would regularly summon Bian into his private quarters, where they feasted and exchanged witty banter.

sentences.zh: 抃尤俊辯，多在侍從，有所顧問，應答如響。

translations.literal: Bian was especially quick and eloquent; he mostly served in attendance; whenever consulted, he replied like an echo.
translations.idiomatic: Bian was especially quick-witted and eloquent and spent most of his time in attendance; whatever was asked of him, he answered without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 性又嗜酒，言雜誹諧，由是彌為太子之所親狎。

translations.literal: By nature he also loved wine; his speech mixed mockery and humor; thereby he became all the more the crown prince's intimate favorite.
translations.idiomatic: He was also fond of wine by nature, and his speech mingled satire and jest; for this reason the crown prince treated him with ever greater familiarity.

sentences.zh: 以其好內典，令撰《法華玄宗》，為二十卷，奏之。

translations.literal: Because he loved Buddhist scriptures, he was ordered to compile Mystic Principles of the Lotus Sutra in twenty scrolls and present it.
translations.idiomatic: Because he was devoted to Buddhist scriptures, the prince ordered him to compile Mystic Principles of the Lotus Sutra in twenty scrolls and submit it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 太子覽而大悅，賞賜優洽，儕輩莫與為比。

translations.literal: The crown prince read it and was greatly pleased; rewards and gifts were generous and warm; none among his peers could compare.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince read it and was greatly pleased; the rewards were generous beyond anything granted to his peers.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，拜秘書監，封漢南縣公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Bian was appointed Director of the Secretariat and enfeoffed as Duke of Hannan county.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, he appointed Bian Director of the Secretariat and enfeoffed him as Duke of Hannan county.

sentences.zh: 帝退朝之後，便命入閣，言宴諷讀，終日而罷。

translations.literal: After the emperor withdrew from court, he would order him into the pavilion; they spoke, feasted, recited, and read until the day ended.
translations.idiomatic: After court each day the emperor would summon him into the privy chambers, where they conversed, feasted, and recited poetry until evening.

sentences.zh: 帝每與嬪後對酒，時逢興會，輒遣命之至，與同榻共席，恩若友朋。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor drank with consorts and the empress, when the mood struck, he would send for Bian to come; they shared couch and mat, their grace like friends.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor drank with his consorts and the empress, and the mood was right, he would send for Bian to join them on the same couch and mat, treating him with the warmth of a close friend.

sentences.zh: 帝猶恨不能夜召，於是命匠刻木偶人，施機關，能坐起拜伏，以像於抃。

translations.literal: The emperor still regretted that he could not summon him at night; therefore he ordered craftsmen to carve a wooden puppet, fitted with mechanisms so it could sit, rise, bow, and prostrate, to resemble Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Still regretting that he could not summon Bian at night, the emperor ordered craftsmen to carve a wooden figure fitted with mechanisms so that it could sit, rise, bow, and prostrate—in Bian's likeness.

sentences.zh: 帝每在月下對酒，輒令宮人置之於座，與相酬酢，而為歡笑。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor drank under the moon, he would have palace women place it on the seat and exchange toasts with it, laughing in merriment.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor drank wine by moonlight, he would have palace women place the puppet at the table so that he could raise cups with it in mock conversation and burst into laughter.

sentences.zh: 從幸揚州，遇疾卒，年六十九。

translations.literal: Accompanying the emperor on a tour to Yangzhou, he fell ill and died, aged sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: While accompanying the emperor on a tour to Yangzhou, he fell ill and died at the age of sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 帝傷惜者久之，贈大將軍，諡曰康。

translations.literal: The emperor mourned and cherished his memory for a long time; posthumously granted Grand General; posthumous title Kang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him for a long time, posthumously appointed him Grand General, and granted him the posthumous title Kang ("Healthy/Peaceful").

sentences.zh: 撰《晉王北伐記》十五卷，有集十卷，行於世。

translations.literal: He wrote Record of the Prince of Jin's Northern Campaign in fifteen scrolls; had collected writings in ten scrolls, circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Record of the Prince of Jin's Northern Campaign in fifteen scrolls; he also left collected writings in ten scrolls, which circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 許善心許善心，字務本，高陽北新城人也。

translations.literal: Xu Shanxin Xu Shanxin, styled Wubén, was a native of Beixinchéng in Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shanxin, whose style name was Wubén, came from Beixinchéng in Gaoyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖懋，梁太子中庶子，始平、天門二郡守、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Mao was Junior Tutor to the Liang crown prince, Prefect of two commanderies—Shiping and Tianmen—and Regular Attendant of the Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Mao had served as Junior Tutor to the Liang crown prince, as Prefect of the Shiping and Tianmen commanderies, and as Regular Attendant of the Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 父亨，仕梁至給事黃門侍郎，在陳曆羽林監、太中大夫、衛尉卿，領大著作。

translations.literal: His father Heng served Liang up to Superintendent Clerk of the Yellow Gate Attendant-in-ordinary; under Chen served as Supervisor of the Forest of Feathered Guards, Grand Master of Palace Attendants, Commandant of the Guard, and concurrently Grand Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: His father Heng had served Liang as Superintendent Clerk of the Yellow Gate Attendant-in-ordinary; under Chen he rose through the posts of Supervisor of the Forest of Feathered Guards, Grand Master of Palace Attendants, and Commandant of the Guard, and concurrently held the post of Grand Compiler.

sentences.zh: 善心九歲而孤，為母范氏所鞠養。

translations.literal: Shanxin was orphaned at nine and was nurtured and raised by his mother, Lady Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxin lost his father at the age of nine and was raised by his mother, Lady Fan.

sentences.zh: 幼聰明有思理，所聞輒能誦記，多聞默識，為當世所稱。

translations.literal: From youth he was clever and thoughtful; whatever he heard he could recite and remember; he heard much and silently retained it, praised by his age.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was clever and thoughtful; whatever he heard he could recite from memory, storing vast learning silently in his mind, and was praised by contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 家有舊書萬餘卷，皆遍通涉。

translations.literal: The family had more than ten thousand scrolls of old books; he thoroughly read through them all.
translations.idiomatic: The family owned more than ten thousand scrolls of old books, all of which he read through thoroughly.

sentences.zh: 十五解屬文，箋上父友徐陵，陵大奇之，謂人曰：「才調極高，此神童也。

translations.literal: At fifteen he mastered composition; sent a letter to his father's friend Xu Ling; Ling was greatly astonished and said to people: "His talent and tone are exceedingly high—this is a divine child."
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he mastered literary composition and sent a letter to his father's friend Xu Ling; Ling was astonished and said to others, "His talent is extraordinary—this is a prodigy."

sentences.zh: 」起家除新安王法曹。

translations.literal: Upon first taking office he was appointed Legal Officer to the Prince of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Upon entering official life he was appointed Legal Officer on the staff of the Prince of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 太子詹事江總舉秀才，對策高第，授度支郎中，轉侍郎，補撰史學士。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince Jiang Zong recommended him as Presented Scholar; in palace examination he ranked high and was appointed Lang of the Revenue Section, transferred to Vice Director, and appointed supplemental Drafting Historian.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince Jiang Zong recommended him as a Presented Scholar; he scored at the top of the palace examination and was appointed Lang of the Revenue Section, later promoted to Vice Director and appointed supplemental Drafting Historian.

sentences.zh: 禎明二年，加通直散騎常侍，聘于隋。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenming he was additionally made Regular Attendant of Direct Communication and Cavalry and sent on embassy to Sui.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Zhenming era he was additionally appointed Regular Attendant of Direct Communication and Cavalry and sent as envoy to Sui.

sentences.zh: 遇高祖伐陳，禮成而不獲反命，累表請辭。

translations.literal: He encountered Gaozu attacking Chen; the rites were completed but he could not receive permission to return; repeatedly memorialized requesting dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: While he was there Gaozu launched his campaign against Chen; though the diplomatic ceremonies were completed, he received no permission to return home and repeatedly memorialized asking to be relieved of his post.

sentences.zh: 上不許，留縶賓館。

translations.literal: The emperor did not permit it and detained him in the guest lodge.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not agree and kept him detained in the guest lodge.

sentences.zh: 及陳亡，高祖遣使告之。

translations.literal: When Chen fell, Gaozu sent an envoy to inform him.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell, Gaozu sent an envoy to inform him of the news.

sentences.zh: 善心衰服號哭於西階之下，藉草東向，經三日。

translations.literal: Shanxin in mourning garments wailed and wept below the western steps; spread grass and faced east; passed three days.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxin put on mourning garb and wailed below the western steps, spreading grass and facing east to mourn; he did so for three days.

sentences.zh: 敕書唁焉。

translations.literal: An imperial letter of condolence was sent to him.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial letter of condolence was sent to comfort him.

sentences.zh: 明日，有詔就館，拜通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: The next day there was an edict at the lodge appointing him Regular Attendant of Direct Communication and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: The next day an edict came to the lodge appointing him Regular Attendant of Direct Communication and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 賜衣一襲。

translations.literal: He was granted one set of robes.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted a set of robes.

sentences.zh: 善心哭盡哀，入房改服，復出北面立，垂涕再拜受詔。

translations.literal: Shanxin wept to the full measure of grief, entered the room to change garments, came out again and stood facing north, tears falling, bowed twice and received the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Having wept his fill, Shanxin withdrew to change his garments, then came out and stood facing north; with tears streaming down he bowed twice and received the edict.

sentences.zh: 明日乃朝，伏泣于殿下，悲不能興。

translations.literal: The next day he attended court, prostrated and wept below the hall, so grieved he could not rise.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he attended court, prostrating himself and weeping below the hall until grief left him unable to rise.

sentences.zh: 上顧左右曰：「我平陳國，唯獲此人。

translations.literal: The emperor looked to those beside him and said: "In pacifying the state of Chen, I gained only this man.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to those beside him and said, "In pacifying Chen, the only prize I truly gained was this man.

sentences.zh: 既能懷其舊君，即是我誠臣也。

translations.literal: Since he can cherish his former ruler, he is my loyal minister.
translations.idiomatic: A man who can still cherish his former ruler is my true loyal minister.

sentences.zh: 」敕以本官直門下省，賜物千段，皁馬二十匹。

translations.literal: " He was ordered to serve at his original rank in the Secretariat Chancellery; granted a thousand rolls of goods and twenty black horses.
translations.idiomatic: " He was ordered to serve at his former rank in the Secretariat Chancellery and was granted a thousand bolts of goods and twenty black horses.

sentences.zh: 從幸太山，還授虞部侍郎。

translations.literal: Accompanying the emperor on a tour to Mount Tai, on return he was appointed Vice Director of the Parks Section.
translations.idiomatic: After accompanying the emperor on a tour to Mount Tai, he was appointed Vice Director of the Parks Section upon their return.

sentences.zh: 十六年，有神雀降于含章闥，高祖召百官賜宴，告以此瑞。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year a divine sparrow descended at the Hanzhang Gate; Gaozu summoned the hundred officials and granted a feast, announcing this auspicious sign.
