translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year a divine sparrow descended at the Hanzhang Gate; Gaozu summoned the hundred officials to a feast and announced this auspicious omen.

sentences.zh: 善心於座請紙筆，制《神雀頌》，其詞曰：

translations.literal: Shanxin at the seat requested paper and brush and composed "Ode to the Divine Sparrow"; its words say:
translations.idiomatic: While still at the feast Shanxin requested paper and brush and composed "Ode to the Divine Sparrow," which reads:

sentences.zh: :臣聞觀象則天，乾元合其德，觀法審地，域大表其尊。

translations.literal: I have heard: observing the emblems, one conforms to Heaven; the primal yang joins its virtue; observing the law, one examines the earth; the great domain displays its dignity.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that by observing the celestial emblems one conforms to Heaven—the primal yang joining its virtue—and by observing the earthly law one examines the land—the great domain displaying its dignity.

sentences.zh: 雨施雲行，四時所以生殺，川流嶽立，萬物於是裁成。

translations.literal: Rain bestowed and clouds moving—thus the four seasons give life and death; rivers flowing and peaks standing—thus the ten thousand things are shaped and completed.
translations.idiomatic: Rain bestowed and clouds adrift are how the four seasons grant life and take it away; rivers flowing and peaks standing are how the ten thousand things are shaped and brought to completion.

sentences.zh: 出震乘離之君，紀雁司鳳之後，玉錘玉鬥而降，金版金縢以傳。

translations.literal: Rulers who emerge from Zhen and mount Li; successors who record geese and manage the phoenix; jade mace and jade dipper descend; golden tablets and golden cords are transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: Sovereigns rise from the trigram Zhen and take the seat of Li; dynasties chronicle the wild geese and maintain the charge of the phoenix—jade mace and jade dipper descend from heaven, and golden tablets bound in golden cords pass the mandate onward.

sentences.zh: 並陶冶性靈，含煦動植，眇玄珠於赤水，寂明鏡乎虛堂。

translations.literal: All refine and mould temperament and spirit, contain warmth in moving and rooted things; seek the dark pearl in the Red Waters, the bright mirror is silent in the empty hall.
translations.idiomatic: All alike refine temperament and spirit and breathe warmth into living and rooted things—seeking the dark pearl in the Red Waters, holding the bright mirror in silent reverence within the empty hall.

sentences.zh: 莫不景福氤氳，嘉貺'集，馳聲南董，越響《雲》《韶》。

translations.literal: None failed to have radiant blessings thick and swarming, good gifts gathering; fame racing Nan and Dong, surpassing the sounds of "Cloud" and "Shao."
translations.idiomatic: None failed to enjoy radiant blessings thick as mist and gracious gifts gathered all around—whose fame outran the historians Nan and Dong and whose triumphs surpassed the music of "Cloud" and "Shao."

sentences.zh: 粵我皇帝之君臨，闡大方，抗太極，負鳳邸，據龍圖。

translations.literal: As for our emperor's lordship over all, he opens the great square, holds up the Grand Ultimate, bears the phoenix mansion, occupies the dragon chart.
translations.idiomatic: As for our emperor's reign over all, he opens the great domain, upholds the Grand Ultimate, bears the phoenix seat, and occupies the dragon chart.

sentences.zh: 不言行焉，攝提建指，不肅清焉，喉鈴啟閉。

translations.literal: Without speaking he acts—the Sheti establishes its pointer; without making austere he is pure—the throat bell opens and closes.
translations.idiomatic: Without issuing commands he governs—the Sheti establishes its pointer; without harsh austerity he brings order—the throat bell opens and closes at his will.

sentences.zh: 括地復夏，截海翦商，就望體其尊，登咸昌其會。

translations.literal: Embracing the earth he restores Xia; cutting the sea and shearing Shang; ascending Wang he embodies its dignity; mounting Xian he flourishes its assembly.
translations.idiomatic: Embracing the earth he restores the legacy of Xia; spanning the seas he trims the domain of Shang—on Mount Wang his dignity is embodied, on Mount Xian his assembly flourishes.

sentences.zh: 綿區浹宇，遐至邇安，騰實飛聲，直暢傍施。

translations.literal: The far regions and near universe are soaked through; the distant come and the near are at peace; solid virtue rises and fame flies; straight and open, extending to all sides.
translations.idiomatic: Far regions and the whole universe are steeped in his grace; the distant arrive and the near dwell in peace—solid virtue rises, fame spreads abroad, straight and openly extending to every side.

sentences.zh: 無體之禮，威儀布政之宮，無聲之樂，綴兆總章之觀。

translations.literal: Rites without form—the palace where dignity is displayed and government spread; music without sound—the hall of Zongzhang where measures and signs are gathered.
translations.idiomatic: Rites without visible form fill the palace where dignity is displayed and government is spread abroad; music without audible sound fills the Hall of Zongzhang where measures and signs are gathered.

sentences.zh: 上庠養老，躬問百年，下土字民，心為百姓。

translations.literal: The upper academy nurtures the aged; he personally inquires after centenarians; below the earth he gives characters to the people; his heart is for the hundred clans.
translations.idiomatic: In the upper academy he nurtures the aged and personally inquires after centenarians; throughout the land he orders the people, holding the common folk in his heart.

sentences.zh: 月棲日浴，熱阪寒門，吹鱗沒羽之荒，赤蛇青馬之裔，解辮請吏，削衽承風。

translations.literal: Where the moon roosts and the sun bathes, Hot Slope and Cold Gate; the wild lands where scales are blown and feathers sink; descendants of the Red Serpent and Green Horse; they loosen braids and request officials, trim lapels and receive the transforming wind.
translations.idiomatic: From lands where the moon roosts and the sun bathes—from Hot Slope and Cold Gate, from the wilds where fish scales are blown and bird feathers sink, from the descendants of the Red Serpent and Green Horse—they loosen their braids and petition for officials, trim their garments and submit to the transforming influence of civilization.

sentences.zh: 豈止呼韓北場，頫勒狼居之岫，熄慎南境，近表不耐之城。

translations.literal: How much more than Huchuan on the northern field, bowing at Langju Mountain; on the southern border of Xishen, recently presenting the city of Bunei.
translations.idiomatic: And not only Huchuan of the northern pastures, bowing before Langju Mountain, or the Xishen of the southern marches, lately presenting the city of Bunei.

sentences.zh: 故使天弗愛道，地寧吝寶，川岳展異，幽明效靈。

translations.literal: Therefore Heaven does not begrudge the Way; Earth how could it withhold treasures; rivers and peaks display wonders; dark and bright manifest spirit-power.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Heaven does not begrudge the Way, nor Earth withhold its treasures; rivers and peaks display wonders, and the realms of dark and light manifest their spiritual power.

sentences.zh: 狎素遊赬，團膏漱醴，半景青赤，孳曆虧盈。

translations.literal: White mingles with crimson, round fat rinsed in sweet wine; half the signs green and red; the calendar waxes and wanes in succession.
translations.idiomatic: White mingles with crimson, blessings round as fat are rinsed in sweet wine; the green and red of the calendar turn, and successive cycles wax and wane.

sentences.zh: 足足懷仁，般般擾義，祥祐之來若此，升隆之化如彼。

translations.literal: Double-footed beasts cherishing benevolence; many-patterned creatures embodying righteousness; auspicious blessings come thus; ascending and descending transformations are like that.
translations.idiomatic: Double-footed beasts cherish benevolence, many-hued creatures embody righteousness—auspicious blessings arrive in such fashion, and the transformations of rise and fall unfold likewise.

sentences.zh: 而登封盛典，雲亭佇白檢之儀，致治成功，柴燎靡玄珪之告。

translations.literal: Yet the grand ceremony of ascending to enfeoff—the Cloud Pavilion awaits the white tally rite; achieving governance and success—the firewood burning finds no dark jade tablet proclamation.
translations.idiomatic: Yet though the grand ceremony of the Feng and Shan sacrifices awaits at Cloud Pavilion with the white tally rite, and though governance is achieved and success attained, the fire-offering finds no dark jade tablet to proclaim it.

sentences.zh: 雖奉常定禮，武騎草文，天子抑而未行，推而不有。

translations.literal: Although the Director of Ceremonies fixed the rites and the Martial Cavalry drafted the documents, the Son of Heaven restrained himself and did not perform them, declined and did not claim them.
translations.idiomatic: Although the Director of Ceremonies fixed the rites and the Martial Cavalry drafted the documents, the Son of Heaven restrained himself and did not carry them out, declining to claim them for himself.

sentences.zh: 允恭克讓，其在斯乎？

translations.literal: Sincere reverence and capacity for yielding—is it not shown here?
translations.idiomatic: Sincere reverence and true capacity for yielding—is it not shown precisely here?

sentences.zh: 七十二君，信蔑如也！

translations.literal: The seventy-two rulers— truly they are as nothing!
translations.idiomatic: Compared with him, the seventy-two ancient rulers are truly as nothing!

sentences.zh: 故神禽顯賁，玄應特昭，白爵主鐵豸之奇，赤爵銜丹書之貴。

translations.literal: Therefore the divine bird displays brilliance; the dark response is specially revealed; the white sparrow lord bears the marvel of the horned beast; the crimson sparrow holds the preciousness of the red writing.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the divine bird displays its splendor and the dark response is specially revealed—the white sparrow bears the marvel of the horned beast, and the crimson sparrow holds the precious dignity of the red writ.

sentences.zh: 班固《神爵》之頌，履武戴文，曹植《嘉爵》之篇，棲庭集牖。

translations.literal: Ban Gu's "Ode to the Divine Sparrow"—treading martial, wearing civil; Cao Zhi's piece "Auspicious Sparrow"—roosting in the courtyard, gathering at the window.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu's "Ode to the Divine Sparrow" celebrated a ruler treading in martial glory and crowned in civil virtue; Cao Zhi's "Auspicious Sparrow" told of birds roosting in the courtyard and gathering at the window.

sentences.zh: 未若于飛武帳，來賀文棕，刷采青蒲，將翱赤罽。

translations.literal: They do not compare with flying to the martial canopy, coming to congratulate at the cultural palm, brushing emerald splendor on green rushes, about to soar in crimson brocade.
translations.idiomatic: None of these compare with this bird's flight to the martial canopy, its arrival to celebrate at the cultural palm—brushing emerald splendor amid green rushes, poised to soar in crimson brocade.

sentences.zh: 玉幾朝禦，取玩軒楯之間，金門旦開，兼留暈翟之鑒。

translations.literal: At the jade throne screen he holds court in the morning; taken for delight between the balustrades; the Golden Gate opens at dawn, also retaining the haloed pheasant's mirror.
translations.idiomatic: At the jade throne screen he holds morning audience, delighting between the balustrades; at dawn the Golden Gate opens, and the haloed pheasant's mirror is likewise retained in view.

sentences.zh: 終古曠世，未或前聞，福召冥徵，得之茲日。

translations.literal: From antiquity through the ages, never before heard; blessings summon hidden signs; obtained on this day.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity through the ages nothing like it was ever heard before; blessings summoned this hidden omen, and it was granted on this very day.

sentences.zh: 歲次上章，律諧大呂，玄枵會節，玄英統時。

translations.literal: The year stands at Shangzhang; the pitch accords with Great Bud; Xuanyuan meets the season-node; Xuanying governs the season.
translations.idiomatic: The year stood at Shangzhang, the pitch accorded with Great Bud, Xuanyuan matched the season's node, and Xuanying governed the season.

sentences.zh: 至尊未明求衣，晨興于含章之殿。

translations.literal: The Most High, before dawn seeking garments, rose early in the Hall of Hanzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Before dawn the Sovereign rose to dress and came forth early in the Hall of Hanzhang.

sentences.zh: 爰有瑞爵，翱翔而下。

translations.literal: Then there was an auspicious sparrow, soaring and descending.
translations.idiomatic: Then an auspicious sparrow appeared, soaring downward.

sentences.zh: 載行載止，當扆甯而徐前，來集來儀，承軒墀而顧步。

translations.literal: Now moving, now stopping; facing the throne screen calmly and slowly advancing; coming to gather, coming with proper bearing; receiving the veranda steps and looking back as it walked.
translations.idiomatic: Now advancing, now pausing, it calmly approached before the throne screen; coming to rest with dignified bearing, it stepped upon the courtyard before the hall and walked with graceful turns.

sentences.zh: 夫瑞者符也，明主之休徵；

translations.literal: An auspicious sign is a token—the excellent lord's felicitous omen;
translations.idiomatic: An auspicious sign is a token—the felicitous omen of an enlightened sovereign;

sentences.zh: 雀者爵也，聖人之大寶。

translations.literal: The sparrow is rank—the sage's great treasure.
translations.idiomatic: The sparrow is rank—the sage's greatest treasure.

sentences.zh: 謹案《考異郵》云：「軒轅有黃爵赤頭，立日傍。

translations.literal: Respectfully examining the Record of Strange Events, it says: "Huangdi had a yellow sparrow with red head, standing beside the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully consulting the Record of Strange Events, it states: "The Yellow Emperor had a yellow sparrow with a red head, standing beside the sun.

sentences.zh: 」占云：「土精之應。

translations.literal: " Divination says: "The response of the spirit of earth.
translations.idiomatic: " Divination reads this as "the response of the spirit of earth.

sentences.zh: 」又《禮稽命徵》云：「祭祀合其宜，則黃爵集。

translations.literal: " Again the Evidential Mandate of Rites says: "When sacrifices accord with what is fitting, the yellow sparrow gathers.
translations.idiomatic: " The Evidential Mandate of Rites also states: "When sacrifices accord with what is fitting, yellow sparrows gather.

sentences.zh: 」昔漢集泰畤之殿，魏下文昌之宮，一見雍丘之祠，三入平東之府，並旁觀回矚，事陋人微，奚足稱矣。

translations.literal: " Formerly Han gathered at the Tai altar hall, Wei descended at the Wenchang palace; once appearing at the Yongqiu shrine, thrice entering the Pingdong storehouse—all observed from the side and looked back; the events were petty and the persons insignificant; how could they be worth mentioning.
translations.idiomatic: " In Han the bird once appeared at the Tai altar hall; in Wei it descended at the Wenchang palace—once at the Yongqiu shrine, thrice at the Pingdong treasury—all merely observed from the sidelines. Those occasions were petty and the men involved insignificant—how could they be worth mentioning?

sentences.zh: 抑又聞之，不刳胎剖卵，則鸞鳳馴鳴；

translations.literal: I also hear that without cutting open wombs and splitting eggs, then the luan and phoenix tame and sing;
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard that if one does not cut open wombs or break eggs, the luan and phoenix come tame and sing;

sentences.zh: 不漉浸焚原，則螭龍盤蜿。

translations.literal: Without draining ponds and burning marshes, then the hornless dragon and dragon coil and wind.
translations.idiomatic: and if one does not drain ponds or burn marshlands, the hornless dragon and dragon coil and writhe in peace.

sentences.zh: 是知陛下止殺，故飛走宅心，皇慈好生，而浮潛育德。

translations.literal: Thus one knows Your Majesty stops killing; therefore flying and running creatures make their home in his heart; imperial compassion loves life, and floating and hidden beings nurture virtue.
translations.idiomatic: From this one knows that because Your Majesty has ceased killing, flying and running creatures have found a home in your heart; because imperial compassion cherishes life, creatures of water and depth alike nurture your virtue.

sentences.zh: 臣面奉綸綍，垂示休祥，預承嘉宴，不勝藻躍。

translations.literal: Your subject face to face received the imperial command, was shown the felicitous sign, beforehand received the fine feast— cannot contain the flowering leap.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject received your command face to face, was shown this felicitous omen, and was honored with this fine feast—I cannot contain my flourishing joy.

sentences.zh: 李虔僻處西土，陸機少長東隅，微臣慚於往賢，逢時盛乎曩代，輒竭庸瑣，敢獻頌云：

translations.literal: Li Qian dwelt obscurely in the western lands; Lu Ji from youth grew in the eastern corner; this petty subject is shamed before past worthies, encountering times more glorious than former ages; I rashly exhaust my petty trifles and dare present this ode, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Li Qian lived obscurely in the western lands and Lu Ji grew up in the eastern marches—your humble servant is shamed before such past worthies, yet encounters an age more glorious than any former dynasty; I have exhausted my poor talents and dare present this ode:

sentences.zh: ::太素式肇，大德資生，功玄不器，道要無名。

translations.literal: The Grand Simplicity forms the beginning; great virtue nourishes life; merit is dark and not constrained; the Way's essentials are nameless.
translations.idiomatic: From the Grand Simplicity the age begins; great virtue nourishes life—merit is profound and unbounded, the essentials of the Way beyond naming.

sentences.zh: 質文鼎革，沿習因成，祥圖瑞史，赫赫明明。

translations.literal: Substance and ornament change by the cauldron; following custom thus formed; auspicious charts and felicitous histories— brilliant and bright.
translations.idiomatic: Substance and ornament shift as the cauldron turns; customs follow and take form—auspicious charts and felicitous histories blaze bright and clear.

sentences.zh: 天保大定，於鑠我君，武義乃武，文教惟文。

translations.literal: Heaven protects and great stability; how radiant our lord; martial righteousness is martial, civil teaching is civil.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven protects and great stability reign—how radiant our sovereign! In martial affairs he is truly martial; in civil teaching he is truly civil.

sentences.zh: 橫塞宇宙，旁凝射、汾，軒物重造，姚風再薰。

translations.literal: Spanning and blocking the cosmos; on the side coagulating at She and Fen; the Xuan ware newly made; the Yao wind again perfumed.
translations.idiomatic: He spans and fills the cosmos, gathering strength at She and Fen—the vessels of the sage-kings are remade, and the transforming wind of Yao is breathed anew.

sentences.zh: 煥發王策，昭彰帝道，御地七神，飛天五老。

translations.literal: Brilliantly issuing the royal policies; clearly manifesting the imperial Way; governing earth—the seven spirits; flying heaven—the five elders.
translations.idiomatic: Brilliantly he issues royal policies and clearly manifests the imperial Way—commanding the seven spirits of earth and summoning the five elders of heaven.

sentences.zh: 山祗吐秘，河靈孕寶，黑羽升壇，青鱗伏皁。

translations.literal: The mountain spirit exhales secrets; the river spirit gestates treasures; black feather ascends the altar; green scales crouch on the dark soil.
translations.idiomatic: Mountain spirits exhale their secrets, river spirits gestate their treasures—black-feathered omens ascend the altar and green-scaled signs crouch upon the dark earth.

sentences.zh: 丹烏流火，白雉從風，棲阿德劭，鳴岐祚隆。

translations.literal: The crimson crow streams fire; the white pheasant follows the wind; roosting at noble virtue's peak; singing at Qi's base— fortune flourishes.
translations.idiomatic: The crimson crow streams fire, the white pheasant follows the wind—they roost where virtue reaches its height and sing at the base of Mount Qi, where fortune flourishes.

sentences.zh: 未如神爵，近賀王宮，五靈何有，百福攸同。

translations.literal: Not like the divine sparrow, nearly congratulating the royal palace; what of the five spirits; a hundred blessings all together.
translations.idiomatic: None match this divine sparrow, come to celebrate at the royal palace—what need of the five spirits when a hundred blessings gather as one?

sentences.zh: 孔圖獻赤，荀文表白，節節奇音，行行瑞跡。

translations.literal: Kong's chart presented crimson; Xun's writing declared white; node by node strange sounds; line by line auspicious tracks.
translations.idiomatic: Kong's charts offered crimson, Xun's writings declared white—at every turn strange music sounds, at every step auspicious tracks appear.

sentences.zh: 化玉黼扆，銜環陛戟，上天之命，明神所格。

translations.literal: Transforming to jade at the embroidered screen; holding the ring at the hall steps and halberds; Heaven's command; the bright spirits who arrive.
translations.idiomatic: It transforms to jade before the embroidered throne screen, holds the ring at the hall steps among the halberds— Heaven's command, the bright spirits come to attend.

sentences.zh: 綏應在旃，伊臣預焉，永緝韋素，方流管弦。

translations.literal: The calm response is on the banner; this subject participates therein; forever compiling on plain silk; now flowing through strings and pipes.
translations.idiomatic: The calm response rests upon the banner—and your servant shares in it; forever to compile on plain silk, now to flow through strings and pipes.

sentences.zh: 頌歌不足，蹈儛無宣，臣拜稽首，億萬斯年。

translations.literal: Eulogy and song are insufficient; dancing cannot express it; your subject bows and kowtows— ten thousand myriad years.
translations.idiomatic: Eulogy and song fall short, dance cannot convey it—your subject bows and kowtows: may you reign for ten thousand myriad years!

sentences.zh: 頌成，奏之，高祖甚悅，曰：「我見神雀，共皇后觀之。

translations.literal: When the ode was complete, he presented it; Gaozu was greatly pleased and said: "I saw the divine sparrow and watched it together with the empress.
translations.idiomatic: When the ode was finished Shanxin presented it; Gaozu was greatly pleased and said, "I saw the divine sparrow and watched it together with the empress.

sentences.zh: 今旦召公等入，適述此事，善心於座始知，即能成頌，文不加點，筆不停毫，常聞此言，今見其事。

translations.literal: This morning I summoned you all in and had just described this matter; Shanxin at the seat only then learned of it, yet was able to complete the ode— the text needed no corrections, the brush never paused; I often heard this saying, today I see the thing itself.
translations.idiomatic: This morning I summoned you here and had just begun to describe the event; Shanxin only then learned of it from his seat at the feast, yet completed the ode at once—without emendation, without the brush pausing. I have often heard such praise said of men of letters; today I have seen it with my own eyes.

sentences.zh: 」因賜物二百段。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he granted two hundred rolls of goods.
translations.idiomatic: " He then granted two hundred bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 十七年，除秘書丞。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was appointed Assistant Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was appointed Assistant Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 于時秘藏圖籍尚多淆亂，善心放阮孝緒《七錄》，更制《七林》，各為總敘，冠於篇首。

translations.literal: At that time the secret repository of charts and books was still much confused; Shanxin modeled himself on Ruan Xiaoxu's Seven Records and newly compiled Seven Forests, each with a general preface placed at the head of the section.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the imperial library's charts and books remained largely disordered; Shanxin drew on Ruan Xiaoxu's Seven Records to compile a new work, Seven Forests, providing a general preface for each category at the head of every section.

sentences.zh: 又於部錄之下，明作者之意，區分其類例焉。

translations.literal: Again, beneath the catalog of each section, he clarified the authors' intentions and distinguished their categories and examples.
translations.idiomatic: Beneath the catalog of each section he also clarified each author's intent and distinguished categories and precedents.

sentences.zh: 又奏追李文博、陸從典等學者十許人，正定經史錯謬。

translations.literal: Again he memorialized to recall some ten scholars such as Li Wenbo and Lu Congdian to correct errors in the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized requesting that some ten scholars, including Li Wenbo and Lu Congdian, be recalled to correct errors in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 仁壽元年，攝黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Renshou he served as Acting Vice Director of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Renshou era he served as Acting Vice Director of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 二年，加攝太常少卿，與牛弘等議定禮樂，秘書丞、黃門，並如故。

translations.literal: In the second year he was additionally made Acting Vice Minister of the Chamberlain for Ceremonials; with Niu Hong and others deliberated and fixed rites and music; Secretary Assistant and Yellow Gate posts both remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was additionally appointed Acting Vice Minister of the Chamberlain for Ceremonials; together with Niu Hong and others he deliberated on rites and music, while retaining his posts as Assistant Director of the Secretariat and Vice Director of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 四年，留守京師。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he remained behind to guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was left behind to serve as custodian of the capital.

sentences.zh: 高祖崩于仁壽宮，煬帝秘喪不發，先易留守官人，出除岩州刺史。

translations.literal: Gaozu died at Renshou Palace; Emperor Yang kept the mourning secret and did not announce it; first replaced the officials left behind as custodians; issued appointment as Prefect of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu died at Renshou Palace, Emperor Yang concealed the death and delayed the announcement; he first replaced the capital custodians, then issued Shanxin an appointment as Prefect of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 逢漢王諒反，不之官。

translations.literal: Meeting Prince of Han Liang's rebellion, he did not go to his post.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Han Yang Liang rose in rebellion, he never took up the appointment.

sentences.zh: ，轉禮部侍郎，奏薦儒者徐文遠為國子博士，包愷、陸德明、褚徽、魯世達之輩並加品秩，授為學官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites, memorialized recommending the Confucian Xu Wenyuan as Erudite of the Directorate of Education; Bao Kai, Lu Deming, Chu Hui, Lu Shida and the like all received raised rank and titles, appointed as instructors.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites and memorialized recommending the scholar Xu Wenyuan as Erudite of the Directorate of Education; Bao Kai, Lu Deming, Chu Hui, Lu Shida, and others were all promoted in rank and appointed instructors.

sentences.zh: 其年，副納言楊達為冀州道大使，以稱旨，賜物五百段。

translations.literal: That year, served as deputy to Palace Aide Yang Da as Commissioner of the Jizhou Circuit; for pleasing the emperor's intent, granted five hundred bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: That year he served as deputy to Palace Aide Yang Da, Commissioner of the Jizhou Circuit; because he pleased the emperor, he was granted five hundred bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 左衛大將軍宇文述每旦借本部兵數十人以供私役，常半日而罷。

translations.literal: Left Guard General Yuwen Shu every morning borrowed several dozen men from his command for private service, usually dismissed after half a day.
translations.idiomatic: Left Guard General Yuwen Shu borrowed several dozen soldiers from his command every morning for private labor, usually releasing them after half a day.

sentences.zh: 攝御史大夫梁毗奏劾之。

translations.literal: Acting Censor-in-Chief Liang Pi memorialized impeaching him.
translations.idiomatic: Acting Censor-in-Chief Liang Pi memorialized an impeachment against him.

sentences.zh: 上方以腹心委述，初付法推，千餘人皆稱被役。

translations.literal: The emperor at the time entrusted Yuwen Shu as a confidant; initially ordered legal investigation; over a thousand all said they had been conscripted for labor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had entrusted Yuwen Shu as a close confidant; when the case was first referred for legal investigation, more than a thousand men all testified that they had been pressed into service.

sentences.zh: 經二十餘日，法官候伺上意，乃言役不滿日，其數雖多，不合通計，縱令有實，亦當無罪。

translations.literal: After more than twenty days, the judges watched the emperor's intent and then said the labor did not fill a full day; though the number was large, they should not be counted in total; even if true, he should be exempt from guilt.
translations.idiomatic: After more than twenty days the judges, reading the emperor's mood, ruled that the labor had not filled a full day; though the number was large, the days could not be totaled together, and even if the facts were true, Yuwen Shu should be held guiltless.

sentences.zh: 諸兵士聞之，更雲初不被役。

translations.literal: The soldiers heard this and further said they had never been conscripted in the first place.
translations.idiomatic: When the soldiers heard this, they changed their testimony and claimed they had never been conscripted at all.

sentences.zh: 上欲釋之，付議虛實，百僚咸議為虛。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to release him; entrusted discussion of truth versus falsehood; all officials argued it was false.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to exonerate him and ordered a deliberation on whether the charges were true or false; the officials all declared them false.

sentences.zh: 善心以為述于仗衛之所抽兵私役，雖不滿日，闕于宿衛，與常役所部，情狀乃殊。

translations.literal: Shanxin held that Yuwen Shu, conscripting soldiers from the guard of arms for private labor, though not filling a full day, was deficient in night guard duty—different in circumstance from ordinary labor conscription.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxin argued that Yuwen Shu had drawn soldiers from the palace guard for private service; even if each stint lasted less than a day, it still left the night watch understrength—a very different matter from ordinary conscript labor.

sentences.zh: 又兵多下番，散還本府，分道追至，不謀同辭。

translations.literal: Also many soldiers were off rotation, scattered returning to their original offices; pursued separately along different routes—they did not collude on their statements.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, many of the soldiers had been off rotation and had already scattered back to their home offices; they were tracked down separately along different routes and had no chance to agree on a story.

sentences.zh: 今殆一月，方始翻覆，奸狀分明，此何可舍。

translations.literal: Now nearly a month, only now reversing their testimony; the deceitful circumstances are clear—how can this be set aside?
translations.idiomatic: Nearly a month had passed before their testimony turned; the fraud was plain—how could such a case be dismissed?

sentences.zh: 蘇威、楊汪等二十餘人，同善心之議。

translations.literal: Su Wei, Yang Wang and over twenty others agreed with Shanxin's opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Su Wei, Yang Wang, and more than twenty others sided with Shanxin.

sentences.zh: 其餘皆議免罪。

translations.literal: The rest all argued for exemption from guilt.
translations.idiomatic: All the rest argued that he should be acquitted.

sentences.zh: 煬帝可免罪之奏。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang approved the memorial for exemption from guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang approved the memorial recommending acquittal.

sentences.zh: 後數月，述譖善心曰：「陳叔寶卒，善心與周羅睺、虞世基、袁充、蔡徵等同往送葬。

translations.literal: Months later, Yuwen Shu slandered Shanxin, saying: "When Chen Shubao died, Shanxin together with Zhou Luohou, Yu Shiji, Yuan Chong, Cai Zheng and others all went to attend the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Some months later Yuwen Shu slandered Shanxin, saying, "When Chen Shubao died, Shanxin went with Zhou Luohou, Yu Shiji, Yuan Chong, Cai Zheng, and others to attend the funeral.

sentences.zh: 善心為祭文，謂為陛下，敢於今日加叔寶尊號。

translations.literal: Shanxin wrote the sacrificial text, calling him 'Your Majesty'—daring on this day to add an honorific title to Shubao.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxin composed the sacrificial text and addressed Shubao as 'Your Majesty'—daring, in the present reign, to bestow on him an imperial honorific.

sentences.zh: 」召問有實，自援古例，事得釋，而帝甚惡之。

translations.literal: " Summoned and questioned; found true; he cited ancient precedents on his own behalf; the matter was dismissed, but the emperor greatly hated him for it.
translations.idiomatic: " Shanxin was summoned and questioned; the facts were confirmed, but he cited ancient precedents in his own defense and the matter was dropped—though the emperor came to loathe him for it.

sentences.zh: 又太史奏帝即位之年，與堯時符合，善心議，以國哀甫爾，不宜稱賀。

translations.literal: Also the Grand Astrologer memorialized that the year of the emperor's accession matched the time of Yao; Shanxin argued that national mourning had just begun, inappropriate to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Astrologer memorialized that the year of the emperor's accession matched the era of Yao, Shanxin argued that the realm was still in mourning and congratulations would be inappropriate.

sentences.zh: 述諷御史劾之，左遷給事郎，降品二等。

translations.literal: Yuwen Shu prompted censors to impeach him; demoted to Gentleman Attendant, rank reduced two grades.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Shu prompted the censors to impeach him; Shanxin was demoted to Gentleman Attendant and his rank was lowered two grades.

sentences.zh: 四年，撰《方物志》奏之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he compiled Records of Regional Products and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he compiled the Records of Regional Products and submitted it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 七年，從至涿郡，帝方自禦戎以東討，善心上封事忤旨，免官。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he followed the emperor to Zhuo commandery; the emperor was personally conducting military campaigns eastward; Shanxin submitted a sealed memorial that offended intent; dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he accompanied the emperor to Zhuo commandery while the emperor personally led the eastern campaign; Shanxin submitted a sealed memorial that displeased him and was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 其年復徵為守給事郎。

translations.literal: That year he was recalled again as acting Gentleman Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he was recalled to serve as acting Gentleman Attendant.

sentences.zh: 九年，攝左翊衛長史，從渡遼，授建節尉。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, acting Chief Clerk of the Left Wing Guard; followed crossing the Liao; granted Commandant Bearing the Staff.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he served as acting chief clerk of the Left Wing Guard, followed the emperor across the Liao, and was granted the title Commandant Bearing the Staff.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗言及高祖受命之符，因問鬼神之事，敕善心與崔祖濬撰《靈異記》十卷。

translations.literal: The emperor once spoke of Gaozu's mandate token, then asked about spirits and ghosts; ordered Shanxin and Cui Zujun to compile Records of Miracles and Omens in ten scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Once when the emperor spoke of the token of Gaozu's mandate and then asked about spirits and ghosts, he ordered Shanxin and Cui Zujun to compile the Records of Miracles and Omens in ten scrolls.

sentences.zh: 初，善心父撰著《梁史》，未就而歿。

translations.literal: Initially, Shanxin's father compiled the History of Liang, unfinished when he died.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset Shanxin's father had begun compiling the History of Liang but died before completing it.

sentences.zh: 善心述成父志，修續家書，其《序傳》末，述製作之意曰：

translations.literal: Shanxin fulfilled his father's intent, continued revising the family book; at the end of the Preface and Biography, narrated the intention of the compilation, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Shanxin carried out his father's design, continued the family history, and at the end of the Preface and Biography explained the purpose of the work, saying:

sentences.zh: :謹案太素將萌，洪荒初判，乾儀資始，辰象所以正時，巛載厚生，品物於焉播氣。

translations.literal: Humbly I consider: the Great Origin about to sprout, primordial chaos first divided; the Qian trigram's forms provision the beginning; celestial phenomena thereby correct the seasons; Kun's carriage thickens life; the myriad things therein scatter their vital breath.
translations.idiomatic: Humbly I observe: when primordial chaos first divided and the cosmos began to stir, Heaven's patterns gave the world its beginning, the stars and seasons their measure, Earth its sustaining bulk, and the myriad creatures their breath of life.

sentences.zh: 參三才而育德，肖二統而降靈。

translations.literal: Drawing on the Three Powers to nurture virtue, resembling the Two Mandates in descending numinous power.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven, Earth, and Man together nurture virtue; the two royal lines descend their sacred power.

sentences.zh: 有人民焉，樹之君長，有貴賤矣，為其宗極。

translations.literal: There being the people, a ruler and chief was planted for them; there being noble and base, one was made their apex.
translations.idiomatic: Where there are people, a ruler is set over them; where there are high and low, one is made their summit.

sentences.zh: 保上天之眷命，膺下土之樂推，莫不執大方，振長策，感召風雲，驅馳英俊。

translations.literal: Safeguarding Heaven's favored mandate, receiving the realm's joyful elevation—none failed to grasp the great principle, rouse the long strategy, summon wind and cloud, and drive forth the outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: Those who secured Heaven's favor, who received the willing acclaim of the realm, all grasped the great design, raised far-reaching plans, summoned wind and cloud, and drove forth the worthy.

sentences.zh: 干戈揖讓，取之也殊功，鼎玉龜符，成之也一致。

translations.literal: By arms or by abdication—the taking has different merit; cauldron, jade scepter, and tortoise tally—the completion is one.
translations.idiomatic: Whether empire was won by war or yielded in courtesy, the means differed; yet the cauldron, the jade scepter, and the tortoise tally mark one and the same completion.

sentences.zh: 革命創制，竹素之道稍彰，紀事記言，筆墨之官漸著。

translations.literal: Revolution and institution-making—the way of bamboo and silk gradually emerged; recording events and recording words, the offices of brush and ink gradually took form.
translations.idiomatic: With each revolution and new founding, the way of writing on bamboo and silk grew clearer; as events and words were recorded, the offices of the historian gradually took shape.

sentences.zh: 炎農以往，存其名而漏其跡，黃軒以來，晦其文而顯其用。

translations.literal: From Flame and Farmer onward, names were preserved but traces leaked away; from Yellow Xuan onward, texts were obscured but uses displayed.
translations.idiomatic: From the Flame Emperor and Farmer Emperor onward, names survived but deeds were lost; from the Yellow Emperor onward, texts were hidden yet their purpose remained visible.

sentences.zh: 登丘納麓，具訓誥及典謨，貫昴入房，傳夏正與殷祀。

translations.literal: Ascending the mound to receive the foot of the hill, instructions and edicts and classic counsels were complete; piercing Mao to enter Fang, Xia's calendar and Yin's sacrifices were transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: On Mount Tai the sage received the charge of Heaven and preserved the Instructions and Counsels; through the stars he fixed Xia's calendar and transmitted Yin's rites of sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 洎辨方正位，論時訓功，南北左右，兼四名之別，檮杌乘車，擅一家之稱。

translations.literal: By the time of distinguishing directions and fixing positions, discussing seasons and instructing merit, south, north, left, and right together held fourfold distinctions; Tao Wu rode in a carriage, monopolizing one family's designation.
translations.idiomatic: When directions were fixed and seasons weighed for merit, south, north, left, and right each had its name; yet Tao Wu alone rode in state and claimed a historiographic title for his house alone.

sentences.zh: 國惡雖諱，君舉必書，故賊子亂臣，天下大懼，元龜明鏡，昭然可察。

translations.literal: Though the state's shame was tabooed, the ruler's acts must be written; thus traitorous sons and rebellious ministers made the realm greatly fear; the sacred tortoise and bright mirror—plainly visible for inspection.
translations.idiomatic: Though a state's disgrace may be concealed in speech, a ruler's deeds must be written; thus traitors and rebels fill the world with dread—the sacred tortoise and bright mirror make all plain.

sentences.zh: 及三郊遞襲，五勝相沿，俱稱百穀之主，並以四海自任，重光累德，何世無哉！

translations.literal: At the succession of the three suburban rites, the five victories passing along, all called themselves lords of the hundred grains and took the four seas as their charge; repeated glory and accumulated virtue—what age has lacked them!
translations.idiomatic: As the three suburban rites passed from hand to hand and the five victories followed one upon another, every ruler called himself lord of the hundred grains and master of the four seas—what age has not boasted repeated glory and piled-up virtue?

sentences.zh: :逮有梁之君臨天下，江左建國，莫斯為盛。

translations.literal: When Liang held lordship over the realm, founding a state in the lands east of the Yangtze, none was greater.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang ruled the realm and founded its state east of the Yangtze, no kingdom of the age was greater.

sentences.zh: 受命在於一君，繼統傳乎四主，克昌四十八載，餘祚五十六年。

translations.literal: The mandate received by one lord, succession passed through four sovereigns; flourishing prosperity for forty-eight years, remaining fortune fifty-six years.
translations.idiomatic: One ruler received the mandate; four sovereigns succeeded in turn; the dynasty flourished for forty-eight years and endured in all for fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 武皇帝出自諸生，爰升寶曆，拯百王之弊，救萬姓之危，反澆季之末流，登上皇之獨道。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu came forth from among the scholars, then ascended the precious calendar; rescued the hundred kings' ills, saved the myriad people's peril; reversed the end-tide of a dissolute age, mounted the solitary Way of the Upper Sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu rose from the ranks of scholars to the throne; he rescued the failings of a hundred kings, delivered the people from peril, turned back the ebbing tide of a decadent age, and ascended the exalted Way of the sage-kings.

sentences.zh: 朝多君子，野無遺賢，禮樂必備，憲章咸舉。

translations.literal: The court had many gentlemen; in the wilds no worthy was overlooked; rites and music were complete; regulations and statutes all raised up.
translations.idiomatic: The court abounded in worthy men; no talent was neglected in the land; rites and music were complete and laws and statutes fully enforced.

sentences.zh: 弘深慈於不殺，濟大忍于無刑，蕩蕩巍巍，可為稱首。

translations.literal: Broadening deep kindness in not killing, aiding great forbearance in having no punishments— vast and lofty, worthy to be called foremost.
translations.idiomatic: He extended deep mercy in sparing life and practiced great forbearance in dispensing with punishment—vast and lofty, he may truly be called foremost among rulers.

sentences.zh: 屬陰戎入潁，羯胡侵洛，沸騰磣黷，三季所未聞，掃地滔天，一元之巨厄。

translations.literal: When the northern barbarians entered Ying and the Jie barbarians invaded Luoyang— bubbling up in filth unheard of since the three final ages, sweeping earth and flooding heaven—a calamity of the whole realm.
translations.idiomatic: Then the northern barbarians entered the Ying and the Jie raiders stormed Luoyang—filth and outrage such as the three degenerate ages had never known, a calamity that seemed to sweep the earth and flood the heavens.

sentences.zh: 廊廟有序，翦成狐兔之場，珪帛有儀，碎夫犬羊之手。

translations.literal: The court in good order was sheared into a field of foxes and hares; jade tokens and silks with their ritual were crushed in the hands of dogs and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered halls became fields for foxes and hares; jade tokens and ceremonial silks were trampled in the hands of dogs and sheep.

sentences.zh: 福善積而身禍，仁義在而國亡。

translations.literal: Accumulated blessing for the good yet personal calamity; benevolence and righteousness present yet the state perished.
translations.idiomatic: Blessings for the good were heaped up, yet the ruler himself met disaster; benevolence and righteousness remained, yet the state was lost.

sentences.zh: 豈天道歟？

translations.literal: Was it Heaven's Way?
translations.idiomatic: Was this Heaven's decree?

sentences.zh: 豈人事歟？

translations.literal: Was it human affairs?
translations.idiomatic: Or was it the fault of men?

sentences.zh: 嘗別論之，在《序論》之卷。

translations.literal: Once I argued this separately, in the volume 'Prefatory Discourses.'
translations.idiomatic: I have discussed this at length elsewhere, in the volume Prefatory Discourses.

sentences.zh: :先君昔在前代，早懷述作，凡撰《齊書》為五十卷；

translations.literal: My late father in former ages early cherished literary composition; in all he composed the History of Qi in fifty scrolls;
translations.idiomatic: My late father, in the former dynasty, long cherished the work of writing and composed the History of Qi in fifty scrolls;

sentences.zh: 《梁書》紀傳，隨事勒成，及闕而未就者，《目錄》注為一百八卷。

translations.literal: The annals and biographies of the History of Liang, recorded as events permitted; what remained unfinished—the catalog notes as one hundred eight scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: the annals and biographies of the History of Liang, written as events allowed; what remained unfinished was noted in the catalog as one hundred and eight scrolls.

sentences.zh: 梁室交喪，墳籍銷盡。

translations.literal: When Liang's house perished together, tombs and records were consumed entirely.
translations.idiomatic: When the house of Liang fell, tombs and archives were destroyed together.

sentences.zh: 塚壁皆殘，不准無所盜，帷囊同毀，陳農何以求！

translations.literal: Tomb walls all ruined, Buzun had nothing to steal; curtain bags likewise destroyed—how could Chen Nong seek them out!
translations.idiomatic: Tomb walls lay in ruins, so even Buzun had nothing left to plunder; book bags were burned as well—how could Chen Nong recover what was lost?

sentences.zh: 秦儒既坑，先王之道將墜，漢臣徒請，口授之文亦絕。

translations.literal: Once Qin scholars were buried alive, the former kings' Way was about to fall; Han courtiers only petitioned—the orally transmitted texts likewise perished.
translations.idiomatic: After Qin buried the scholars alive, the Way of the former kings nearly collapsed; Han officials could only petition—the orally transmitted texts perished as well.

sentences.zh: 所撰之書，一時亡散。

translations.literal: The books he composed were at one stroke lost and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: The books he had written were lost and scattered in a single stroke.

sentences.zh: 有陳初建，詔為史官，補闕拾遺，心識口誦。

translations.literal: When Chen was first established, an edict made him Historiographer; mending omissions and gathering lost material, from mind's knowledge and mouth's recitation.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen was first founded, an edict appointed him historiographer; mending omissions and gathering what was lost, he worked from memory and oral recitation.

sentences.zh: 依舊目錄，更加修撰，且成百卷，已有六帙五十八卷，上秘閣訖。

translations.literal: Following the old catalog, he further revised and compiled; nearing one hundred scrolls, already six fascicles and fifty-eight scrolls, submitted to the Secret Archive.
translations.idiomatic: Following the old catalog he continued revising and compiling; nearing one hundred scrolls, he had already completed six fascicles totaling fifty-eight scrolls and submitted them to the Secret Archive.

sentences.zh: :善心早嬰荼蓼，弗荷薪構，太建之末，頻抗表聞，至德之初，蒙授史任。

translations.literal: Shanxin early tasted bitter hardship, did not bear the burden of founding; at the end of Taijian repeatedly submitted memorials to report; at the beginning of Zhide received appointment to historiographic duty.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxin had known hardship from youth and did not share in founding the state; at the end of the Taijian era he repeatedly submitted memorials, and at the beginning of the Zhide era received appointment as historiographer.

sentences.zh: 方願油素採訪，門庭記錄，俯勵弱才，仰成先志；

translations.literal: Just then he wished to take black silk for collecting inquiry, record at door and courtyard, bowing to rouse his weak talent, looking up to fulfill his father's intent;
translations.idiomatic: He hoped to travel with ink and silk to gather materials, to record what came to his door, to bend his modest talent to the task and fulfill his father's design;

sentences.zh: 而單宗少強近，虛室類原、顏，退屏無所交遊，棲遲不求進益。

translations.literal: yet the lone branch had few powerful kin, empty rooms like Yuan and Yan— retired and secluded with none to associate, lingering without seeking advancement.
translations.idiomatic: yet his branch of the family had few powerful connections; his rooms stood empty like those of Yan Hui and Yuan Xian; he lived in retirement without companions and made no effort to advance.

sentences.zh: 假班嗣之書，徒聞其語，給王隱之筆，未見其人。

translations.literal: Borrowing Ban Si's book, only heard his words; given Wang Yin's brush, never saw the man.
translations.idiomatic: He could borrow Ban Si's book but only hear his words secondhand; he might be given Wang Yin's brush yet never meet the man himself.

sentences.zh: 加以庸瑣涼能，孤陋末學，忝職郎署，兼撰《陳史》，致此書延時，未即成續。

translations.literal: Added to this mediocre and trifling ability, solitary and narrow late learning, disgracefully holding office in the Secretariat, concurrently compiling the History of Chen— causing this book to be delayed, not yet completed.
translations.idiomatic: To this were added his mediocre talents, his narrow late learning, his unworthy service in the Secretariat, and his concurrent work on the History of Chen—all of which delayed this book and kept it from completion.

sentences.zh: ，以臺郎入聘，值本邑淪覆，他鄉播遷，行人失時，將命不復。

translations.literal: Sent as Secretariat Gentleman on embassy; just as the capital fell; scattered abroad in another land; the envoy lost his timing; the mission never resumed.
translations.idiomatic: Sent abroad as a secretariat gentleman on embassy, he was caught when the capital fell; scattered to a foreign land, the envoy lost his season and the mission was never resumed.

sentences.zh: 望都亭而長慟，遷別館而懸壺。

translations.literal: Gazing at the capital pavilion he wept long; moved to a separate lodge he hung his gourd.
translations.idiomatic: He gazed toward the capital pavilion and wept bitterly; lodged in a foreign inn, he hung out his gourd as a physician.

sentences.zh: 家史舊書，在後焚蕩。

translations.literal: The family history and old books were afterward burned and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The family history and old books were afterward burned and lost.

sentences.zh: 今止有六十八卷在，又並缺落失次。

translations.literal: Now only sixty-eight scrolls remain, all fragmented and disordered.
translations.idiomatic: Only sixty-eight scrolls survive today, all incomplete and out of order.

sentences.zh: 自入京已來，隨見補葺，略成七十卷。

translations.literal: Since entering the capital, repairing as he found material, roughly completed seventy scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Since coming to the capital he has patched and repaired what he could find, completing roughly seventy scrolls.

sentences.zh: 《四帝紀》八卷，《后妃》一卷，《三太子錄》一卷，為一帙十卷。

translations.literal: Basic Annals of the Four Emperors, eight scrolls; Consorts, one scroll; Record of the Three Crown Princes, one scroll—one fascicle of ten scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Basic Annals of the Four Emperors, eight scrolls; Consorts, one scroll; Record of the Three Crown Princes, one scroll—one fascicle of ten scrolls.

sentences.zh: 《宗室王侯列傳》一帙十卷。

translations.literal: Biographies of Imperial Clansmen, Princes, and Marquises, one fascicle of ten scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Biographies of Imperial Clansmen, Princes, and Marquises, one fascicle of ten scrolls.

sentences.zh: 《具臣列傳》二帙二十卷。

translations.literal: Biographies of Established Ministers, two fascicles of twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Biographies of Established Ministers, two fascicles of twenty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 《外戚傳》一卷，《孝德傳》一卷，《誠臣傳》一卷，《文苑傳》二卷，《儒林傳》二卷，《逸民傳》一卷，《數術傳》一卷，《籓臣傳》一卷，合一帙十卷。

translations.literal: Biographies of Consort Kin, one scroll; Biographies of Filial Virtue, one scroll; Biographies of Loyal Ministers, one scroll; Biographies of Literary Circles, two scrolls; Biographies of the Confucian School, two scrolls; Biographies of Recluses, one scroll; Biographies of Diviners, one scroll; Biographies of Frontier Lords, one scroll—together one fascicle of ten scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Biographies of Consort Kin, one scroll; Biographies of Filial Virtue, one scroll; Biographies of Loyal Ministers, one scroll; Biographies of Literary Circles, two scrolls; Biographies of the Confucian School, two scrolls; Biographies of Recluses, one scroll; Biographies of Diviners, one scroll; Biographies of Frontier Lords, one scroll—together one fascicle of ten scrolls.

sentences.zh: 《止足傳》一卷，《列女傳》一卷，《權幸傳》一卷，《羯賊傳》二卷，《逆臣傳》二卷，《叛臣傳》二卷，《敘傳論述》一卷，合一帙十卷。

translations.literal: Biographies of Those Who Know When to Stop, one scroll; Biographies of Exemplary Women, one scroll; Biographies of the Powerful and Favored, one scroll; Biographies of Jie Bandits, two scrolls; Biographies of Rebellious Ministers, two scrolls; Biographies of Defecting Ministers, two scrolls; Narrative Discourses, one scroll—together one fascicle of ten scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Biographies of Those Who Know When to Stop, one scroll; Biographies of Exemplary Women, one scroll; Biographies of the Powerful and Favored, one scroll; Biographies of Jie Bandits, two scrolls; Biographies of Rebellious Ministers, two scrolls; Biographies of Defecting Ministers, two scrolls; Narrative Discourses, one scroll—together one fascicle of ten scrolls.

sentences.zh: 凡稱史臣者，皆先君所言，下稱名案者，並善心補闕。

translations.literal: Whenever it says 'the historiographer,' it is all the late father's words; where below it says 'Shanxin notes,' all are Shanxin's additions and corrections.
translations.idiomatic: Passages marked 'the historiographer' are all my late father's words; passages marked 'Shanxin notes' are my own additions and corrections.

sentences.zh: 別為《敘論》一篇，託於《敘傳》之末。

translations.literal: Separately composed one piece, 'Discursive Preface,' entrusted to the end of the 'Narrative Biography.'
translations.idiomatic: I have also written a separate Discursive Preface, appended to the end of the Narrative Biography.

sentences.zh: 十年，又從至懷遠鎮，加授朝散大夫。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he again followed the emperor to Huaiyuan garrison and was additionally granted Gentleman for Spreading Illumination.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he again accompanied the emperor to Huaiyuan garrison and was additionally granted the title Gentleman for Spreading Illumination.

sentences.zh: 突厥圍雁門，攝左親衛武賁郎將，領江南兵宿衛殿省。

translations.literal: When the Turks besieged Yanmen, he served as acting Colonel of the Valiant Guards of the Left Guard, leading Jiangnan troops to guard the palace halls by night.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks besieged Yanmen, he served as acting colonel of the Valiant Guards of the Left Guard and led Jiangnan troops in night guard of the palace halls.

sentences.zh: 駕幸江都郡，追敘前勳，授通議大夫。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage visited Jiangdu commandery, past merit was reviewed and he was granted Grand Master for Discussion.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor traveled to Jiangdu commandery, his earlier service was reviewed and he was granted the title Grand Master for Discussion.

sentences.zh: 詔還本品，行給事郎。

translations.literal: An edict restored his original rank while he served as acting Gentleman Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored his original rank while he continued to serve as acting Gentleman Attendant.

sentences.zh: 十四年，化及殺逆之日，隋官盡詣朝堂謁賀，善心獨不至。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, on the day of Yuwen Huaji's regicidal coup, all Sui officials went to the court hall to offer congratulations; Shanxin alone did not come.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, on the day Yuwen Huaji murdered the emperor, every Sui official went to the court hall to offer congratulations—Shanxin alone did not appear.

sentences.zh: 許弘仁馳告之曰：「天子已崩，宇文將軍攝政，合朝文武莫不咸集。

translations.literal: Xu Hongren rushed to tell him: "The Son of Heaven is dead; General Yuwen holds regency; all the court's civil and military officials have gathered.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Hongren rode to tell him, "The Son of Heaven is dead; General Yuwen holds the regency; every civil and military official at court has already assembled.

sentences.zh: 天道人事，自有代終，何預于叔而低徊若此！

translations.literal: Heaven's Way and human affairs have their own succession—what concern is it of yours, uncle, to hesitate thus!
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and men each have their turning—what is that to you, uncle, that you linger so?

sentences.zh: 」善心怒之，不肯隨去。

translations.literal: " Shanxin angrily refused and would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: " Shanxin grew angry and refused to go.

sentences.zh: 弘仁反走上馬，泣而言曰：「將軍于叔全無惡意，忽自求死，豈不痛哉！

translations.literal: Hongren turned, mounted his horse, and weeping said: "The general means you no harm at all; yet you suddenly seek death—how is that not pitiable!
translations.idiomatic: Hongren wheeled his horse and, weeping, cried, "The general bears you no ill will at all, yet you would throw your life away—how can that not grieve me?

sentences.zh: 」還告唐奉義，以狀白化及，遣人就宅執至朝堂。

translations.literal: " Returning he told Tang Fengyi; reporting the matter to Huaji, Huaji sent men to his residence to seize him and bring him to the court hall.
translations.idiomatic: " He returned and reported to Tang Fengyi, who told Huaji; Huaji sent men to seize Shanxin at his house and bring him to the court hall.

sentences.zh: 化及令釋之，善心不舞蹈而出。

translations.literal: Huaji ordered him released; Shanxin left without performing the ritual dance of submission.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji ordered him released, but Shanxin departed without performing the ritual dance of submission.

sentences.zh: 化及目送之曰：「此人大負氣。

translations.literal: Huaji watched him go and said: "This man is full of pride.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji watched him leave and said, "This man is stiff with pride.

sentences.zh: 」命捉將來，罵云：「我好欲放你，敢如此不遜！

translations.literal: " He ordered him seized and brought back, cursing: "I truly wished to release you—how dare you be so insolent!
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered him seized and brought back, shouting, "I meant to spare you—how dare you show such insolence!

sentences.zh: 」其黨輒牽曳，因遂害之，時年六十一。

translations.literal: " His followers dragged him off, and so he was killed—aged sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: " His followers dragged him away and killed him. He was sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 及越王稱制，贈左光祿大夫、高陽縣公，諡曰文節。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yue assumed power, Shanxin was posthumously granted Left Grand Master of the Bright Hall and Duke of Gaoyang, with the posthumous name Wenjie.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yue assumed power, Shanxin was posthumously granted Left Grand Master of the Bright Hall and Duke of Gaoyang, with the posthumous title Wenjie.

sentences.zh: 善心母范氏，梁太子中舍人孝才之女，少寡養孤，博學有高節。

translations.literal: Shanxin's mother Lady Fan was daughter of Xiao Taizhong Sheren Xiaocai of Liang; widowed young, she raised her orphan alone; broadly learned with lofty integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxin's mother, Lady Fan, was the daughter of Liang's Palace Secretariat Gentleman Xiaocai; widowed young, she raised her son alone; she was broadly learned and of lofty character.

sentences.zh: 高祖知之，敕尚食每獻時新，常遣分賜。

translations.literal: Gaozu knew of her; ordered the Imperial Kitchen whenever seasonal delicacies were presented to send a portion to her.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu learned of her and ordered that whenever the Imperial Kitchen presented seasonal delicacies, a portion be sent to her.

sentences.zh: 嘗詔範入內，侍皇后講讀，封永樂郡君。

translations.literal: Once an edict summoned Lady Fan into the palace to attend the empress in lectures and reading; she was enfeoffed as Lady of Yongle commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Once she was summoned by edict into the palace to attend the empress in lectures and reading, and was enfeoffed as Lady of Yongle commandery.

sentences.zh: 及善心遇禍，範年九十有二，臨喪不哭，撫柩曰：「能死國難，我有兒矣。

translations.literal: When Shanxin met disaster, Lady Fan was ninety-two; facing the coffin she did not weep, stroking the bier said: "To die for the state's peril—I have such a son.
translations.idiomatic: When Shanxin met his death, Lady Fan was ninety-two; at the coffin she did not weep, but stroking the bier said, "To die in the nation's crisis—I have borne such a son.

sentences.zh: 」因臥不食，後十餘日亦終。

translations.literal: " Thereupon she took to her bed and ate nothing; after ten-odd days she too died.
translations.idiomatic: " Then she took to her bed and refused food; more than ten days later she died as well.

sentences.zh: 李文博博陵李文博，性貞介鯁直，好學不倦，至於教義名理，特所留心。

translations.literal: Li Wenbo of Boling—Li Wenbo's nature was upright, uncompromising, and straight; he loved learning without tiring; as to moral teaching and the principles of names, he especially kept them in mind.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wenbo of Boling was upright, uncompromising, and plain-spoken; he loved learning tirelessly and gave special heed to moral teaching and the principles of names.

sentences.zh: 每讀書至治亂得失，忠臣列士，未嘗不反覆吟玩。

translations.literal: Whenever he read of the rise and fall of order and disorder, loyal ministers and exemplary men, he never failed to turn the passages over and savor them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he read of the rise and fall of states, or of loyal ministers and exemplary men, he would turn the passages over again and again in silent admiration.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，為羽騎尉，特為吏部侍郎薛道衡所知，恆令在聽事帷中披檢書史，並察己行事。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era he served as Feathered Cavalry Guard; he was especially known to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel Xue Daoheng, who constantly had him within the curtain of the reception hall examining books and histories and observing his own conduct.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaihuang era he served as Feathered Cavalry Guard and came to the special notice of Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel Xue Daoheng, who kept him behind the curtain in the reception hall to examine books and histories and observe his own conduct.

sentences.zh: 若遇治政善事，即抄撰記錄，如選用疏謬，即委之臧否。

translations.literal: If he encountered good governance he copied and recorded it; if he found errors in appointments he entrusted his praise or blame.
translations.idiomatic: When he found examples of good governance he copied and recorded them; when he found errors in appointments he did not hesitate to praise or blame.

sentences.zh: 道衡每得其語，莫不欣然從之。

translations.literal: Daoheng whenever he received his words never failed to follow them with pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Daoheng heard his counsel, he gladly followed it.

sentences.zh: 後直秘書內省，典校墳籍，守道居貧，晏如也。

translations.literal: Later he served directly in the Secretariat Inner Office, overseeing collation of ancient texts; he kept to the Way and lived in poverty, yet remained at ease.
translations.idiomatic: He later served in the Secretariat Inner Office, where he oversaw the collation of ancient texts; he held to the Way and lived in poverty, yet remained content.

sentences.zh: 雖衣食乏絕，而清操逾厲，不妄通賓客，恆以禮法自處，儕輩莫不敬憚焉。

translations.literal: Though food and clothing were utterly lacking, his pure conduct grew ever stricter; he did not casually receive guests and always regulated himself by ritual propriety, so his peers all respected and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Though he lacked food and clothing, his integrity grew only stricter; he did not receive guests casually and always held himself to ritual propriety, so his peers respected and stood in awe of him.

sentences.zh: 道衡知其貧，每延於家，給以資費。

translations.literal: Daoheng knew of his poverty and often invited him to his home, supplying him with funds.
translations.idiomatic: Daoheng knew he was poor and often had him to his home, providing him with funds.

sentences.zh: 文博商略古今，治政得失，如指諸掌，然無吏幹。

translations.literal: Wenbo discussed and weighed antiquity and the present, the gains and losses of governance, as if pointing to his palm—yet he had no administrative capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbo could discuss antiquity and the present and the gains and losses of governance as clearly as if they lay in his palm—yet he lacked administrative talent.

sentences.zh: 稍遷校書郎。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Collator.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to Collator.

sentences.zh: 後出為縣丞，遂得下考，數歲不調。

translations.literal: Later sent out as Assistant Magistrate, he received a low evaluation and for several years received no new appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Later sent out as Assistant Magistrate, he received a poor performance rating and went several years without a new appointment.

sentences.zh: 道衡為司隸大夫，遇之於東都尚書省，甚嗟湣之，遂奏為從事。

translations.literal: Daoheng became Minister of the Capital Metropolitan Court; encountering him at the Eastern Capital Masters of Writing office, he sighed in deep pity and memorialized to appoint him as Staff Officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Daoheng became Minister of the Capital Metropolitan Court, he met Wenbo at the Eastern Capital office of the Masters of Writing, sighed in pity, and memorialized to appoint him as Staff Officer.

sentences.zh: 因為齊王司馬李綱曰：「今日遂遇文博，得奏用之。

translations.literal: He then said to Li Gang, Military Administrator of the Prince of Qi: "Today I have at last met Wenbo and was able to memorialize for his employment."
translations.idiomatic: He then said to Li Gang, Military Administrator of the Prince of Qi, "Today I have at last met Wenbo and secured a memorial for his appointment."

sentences.zh: 」以為歡笑。

translations.literal: " He spoke this in delight.
translations.idiomatic: He said this with evident delight.

sentences.zh: 其見賞知音如此。

translations.literal: Such was the degree to which he was prized and understood.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which he was held by those who knew him.

sentences.zh: 在洛下，曾詣房玄齡，相送于衢路。

translations.literal: While in Luoyang he once visited Fang Xuanling, who saw him off in the street.
translations.idiomatic: While in Luoyang he once called on Fang Xuanling, who walked with him into the street to see him off.

sentences.zh: 玄齡謂之曰：「公生平志尚，唯在正直，今既得為從事，故應有會素心。

translations.literal: Xuanling said to him: "Your lifelong aspiration has lain solely in uprightness; now that you have become a Staff Officer, you should have opportunity to realize your true heart."
translations.idiomatic: Xuanling said to him, "Your lifelong aspiration has been nothing but uprightness; now that you are a Staff Officer, you should at last be able to act on your true convictions."

sentences.zh: 比來激濁揚清，所為多少？

translations.literal: " In recent times, in stirring the muddy and raising the clear, how much have you accomplished?
translations.idiomatic: " In recent times, in stirring the muddy and lifting the clear, how much have you actually accomplished?"

sentences.zh: 」文博遂奮臂厲聲曰：「夫清其流者必潔其源，正其末者須端其本。

translations.literal: " Wenbo then flung up his arms and said in a stern voice: "He who clears the stream must cleanse the source; he who straightens the branch must square the root."
translations.idiomatic: Wenbo flung up his arms and said sharply, "He who clears the stream must cleanse the source; he who straightens the branch must square the root."

sentences.zh: 今治源混亂，雖日免十貪郡守，亦何所益！

translations.literal: " Today the source of government is chaotic; even if ten greedy prefects were dismissed daily, what good would it do!
translations.idiomatic: " Today the sources of government are chaotic; even if ten corrupt prefects were dismissed every day, what good would it do!"

sentences.zh: 」其瞽直疾惡，不知忌諱，皆此類也。

translations.literal: " His blindness to straight speaking, his hatred of evil, and his ignorance of taboo were all of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: His bluntness, his hatred of evil, and his disregard for what was forbidden were all of this kind.

sentences.zh: 于時朝政浸壞，人多贓賄，唯文博不改其操，論者以此貴之。

translations.literal: At that time court governance was gradually corrupt and many took bribes; only Wenbo did not alter his conduct, and critics for this reason honored him.
translations.idiomatic: Court governance was then gradually decaying and many took bribes; Wenbo alone did not alter his conduct, and critics honored him for it.

sentences.zh: 遭離亂播遷，不知所終。

translations.literal: He met with the turmoil of dispersal in chaos and his end is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: He was swept away in the chaos of dispersal, and his final fate is unknown.

sentences.zh: 初，文博在內校書，虞世基子亦在其內，盛飾容服，而未有所卻。

translations.literal: Earlier, while Wenbo was collating books within the palace, the son of Yu Shiji was also among them, richly adorned in dress, yet had accomplished nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Wenbo was collating books in the palace, Yu Shiji's son was also among the collators, richly dressed yet having accomplished nothing.

sentences.zh: 文博因從容問之年紀，答云：「十八。

translations.literal: Wenbo calmly asked his age; he answered: "Eighteen."
translations.idiomatic: Wenbo calmly asked his age; the youth answered, "Eighteen."

sentences.zh: 」文博乃謂之曰：「昔賈誼當此之年，議論何事？

translations.literal: " Wenbo then said to him: "When Jia Yi was this age, what affairs did he debate?
translations.idiomatic: Wenbo then said to him, "When Jia Yi was this age, what great affairs was he debating?

sentences.zh: 君今徒事儀容，故何為者！

translations.literal: " You now attend only to appearance and dress—what is that for!
translations.idiomatic: " You now attend only to appearance and dress—for what purpose!"

sentences.zh: 」又秦孝王妃生男，高祖大喜，頒賜群官各有差。

translations.literal: " Also, when the consort of Prince Xiao of Qin bore a son, Gaozu was greatly pleased and distributed rewards to the officials, each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: When the consort of Prince Xiao of Qin bore a son, Gaozu was greatly pleased and distributed rewards among the officials according to rank.

sentences.zh: 文博家道屢空，人謂其悅，乃云：「賞罰之設，功過所歸，今王妃生男，于群官何事，乃妄受賞也！

translations.literal: Wenbo's household was repeatedly empty; people thought he would be pleased, but he said: "Rewards and punishments exist for merit and fault; today the prince's consort bore a son—what affair is that of the officials, that we should receive rewards in vain!"
translations.idiomatic: Wenbo's household was repeatedly destitute; people assumed he would be pleased, but he said, "Rewards and punishments reflect merit and fault; the prince's consort bore a son today—what affair is that of the officials, that we should accept rewards without cause!"

sentences.zh: 」其循名責實，錄過計功，必使賞罰不濫，功過無隱者皆爾。

translations.literal: " In adhering to names and demanding realities, recording faults and reckoning merit, he was determined that reward and punishment should not overflow and that merit and fault should not be hidden—all were like this.
translations.idiomatic: In adhering to names and demanding realities, recording faults and reckoning merit, he insisted that rewards and punishments should not be misapplied and that merit and fault should not be concealed—his conduct was always of this kind.

sentences.zh: 文博本為經學，後讀史書，于諸子及論尤所該洽。

translations.literal: Wenbo originally studied the classics, later read historical works, and among the masters and discourses was especially comprehensive.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbo had originally studied the classics and later read historical works; among the masters and various treatises he was especially well versed.

sentences.zh: 性長議論，亦善屬文，著《治道集》十卷，大行於世。

translations.literal: By nature he excelled at discourse and was also skilled at composition; he wrote Ten Scrolls on the Governance of the Way, which circulated widely in the world.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he excelled at discourse and was skilled at literary composition; he wrote Ten Scrolls on the Governance of the Way, which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：明克讓、魏澹等，或博學洽聞，詞藻贍逸，既稱燕趙之俊，實曰東南之美。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Ming Kerang, Wei Dan, and the others were either broadly learned and comprehensive in knowledge, or rich and flowing in diction—they were called the talents of Yan and Zhao and truly the beauties of the southeast.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer remarks: Ming Kerang, Wei Dan, and the others were either broadly learned or gifted with lush prose—they were acclaimed as talents of Yan and Zhao and truly as the finest scholars of the southeast.

sentences.zh: 所在見寶，咸取祿位，雖無往非命，蓋亦道有存焉。

translations.literal: Wherever they went they were treasured and all took salary and rank; though not every turn of fate was favorable, surely the Way had its place in them.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever they went they were valued and all obtained office and rank; though fortune did not always favor them, the Way surely had a place in their lives.

sentences.zh: 澹之《魏書》，時稱簡正，條例詳密，足傳於後。

translations.literal: Dan's History of Wei was at the time called concise and correct, its regulations detailed and close, sufficient to transmit to posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Dan's History of Wei was acclaimed in its day as concise and correct, with detailed and rigorous regulations, sufficient to pass to posterity.

sentences.zh: 此外諸子，各有記述，雖道或小大，皆志在立言，美矣。

translations.literal: Beyond this, the various subjects each had their writings; though their paths differed in scale, all aspired to establish words—how fine.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond this, each of the others left writings of his own; though their paths differed in scope, all aspired to establish a literary legacy—admirable indeed.
